detail.abstract: I propose Citizens' Equity, a simple mechanism wherein corporations contribute fractions of their capital liabilities to a sovereign fund issuing one share to each citizen. The percentages of those total liabilities contributed are computed from two variables, a policy variable tracking the level of (AI-related or other) distress in labor markets, and the  company's percentage domestic share of global revenue.  CE is shown to dominate UBI and tariffs on welfare grounds, and the bi-variate mechanism generates an international cooperative equilibrium leading to multilateral adoption with converging policy variables. An appendix develops methods to compute contributions within complex supply chains.

title: U.S.-China Innovation Competition
affiliations: University of Southern California - Marshall School of Business - Finance and Business Economics Department, UNSW Business School and Dartmouth College - Tuck School of Business

detail.title: U.S.-China Innovation Competition
detail.abstract: We examine how foreign information access affects competition in innovation. We construct measures of Chinese information-gathering capacity based on industry geography and internet penetration. They predict actual Chinese-user downloads of U.S. firm filings. Increases in Chinese information access are followed by lower U.S. firm R&D, patent values, and patent grants. Chinese firms increase patenting in the same technology areas and cite more affected U.S. firms' prior patents. The effects are stronger in more contested markets and in industries receiving Chinese government support. Placebo tests do not produce similar results. The evidence is consistent with Chinese innovation competition reducing U.S. innovation.

title: "Cognitive Warfare and Targeting Societal Cohesion: A Critical Analytical Study of Israeli Practices in the Regional Environment"

detail.title: "Cognitive Warfare and Targeting Societal Cohesion: A Critical Analytical Study of Israeli Practices in the Regional Environment"
detail.abstract: The global conflict landscape has shifted from traditional battlefields to "Cognitive Warfare." This study examines how Israeli security establishments employ cognitive operations targeting the Arab region, specifically Egypt, as an alternative to traditional deterrence. It traces the doctrine's evolution from "Hasbara" to the "re-engineering of consciousness," analyzing the AI and cyber-intelligence infrastructure (notably Unit 8200) used to manipulate perceptions and exploit cognitive biases. The research argues that these operations aim to degrade "Societal Cohesion" by targeting the state's psychological foundations. Finally, the paper evaluates the structural failures of these campaigns post-October 2023 and proposes strategic frameworks for building "Societal Cognitive Immunity" as a proactive national security defense against information manipulation.

title: The Anatomy of a Decentralized Prediction Market: Microstructure Evidence from the Polymarket Order Book

detail.title: The Anatomy of a Decentralized Prediction Market: Microstructure Evidence from the Polymarket Order Book

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study analyzes publicly observable order-book and trade data. The Polymarket public WebSocket feed broadcasts limit-order-book state updates that any client can subscribe to; the Polygon OrderFilled events are public on-chain transactions recorded by the Polymarket CTF Exchange smart contract. No private user data was collected. Counterparty addresses on chain are pseudonymous public-key identifiers; we use them only to compute maker-wallet concentration (Section 5.4) and a self-counterparty wash-share lower bound (Section 5.7), without attempting to deanonymise any wallet.
declarations.funderStatement: The author declares study is self funded.

detail.abstract: We study the microstructure of Polymarket, the largest on-chain prediction market, using a continuous tick-level archive of the public WebSocket order-book feed (30 billion events over 52 days) joined to the authoritative on-chain trade record. On a pre-registered stratified panel of 600 markets we report eight stylized facts: a longshot spread premium; a depth-concentration profile closer to a uniform geometric grid than to the top-of-book pattern often assumed for prediction markets; a null block-clock alignment effect; broad maker-wallet diversity with a concentrated tail; category-conditional differences in effective spread; a sub-50 ms median archive-ingestion delay with a multi-second tail; a self-counterparty wash share with median 1% and a 22% upper tail, where the comparison to the network-classifier benchmarks of Cong et al. [2023] on unregulated cryptocurrency token exchanges is a sanity bound rather than an apples-to-apples reference because the venues face different wash incentives; and a depth-decay-near-resolution effect with a within-category slope of 0.55 on log seconds-to-close (t = 3.85). The paper also contributes a measurement result: trade direction inferred from Polymarket's public order-book feed agrees with on-chain ground truth only ∼59% of the time (volume-weighted across the top-100 stratum and four disjoint 7-day windows; panel mean 0.615, market-clustered bootstrap 95% CI [0.58, 0.65], IQR [0.53, 0.68]), barely above the 50% chance baseline that direction-dependent microstructure measures need. On the comparable subset of the top-100 panel, the effective half-spread changes sign between feed- and on-chain trade directions on 67% of markets in the first 7-day window (50% in a second non-overlapping window), and Kyle's λ changes sign on 60% (43% in the second window); both windows fail to recover the on-chain sign at anything close to the ∼80% rate that Lee-Ready achieves on equity venues. Microstructure work on Polymarket therefore needs to source trade direction from on-chain OrderFilled events; we release a replication package that performs the join.

title: Segmentation-Guided Quantitative Evaluation of CNN Explanation Fidelity on Out-of-Distribution Chest X-Rays
affiliations: University of Central Punjab, University of Central Punjab, Newman University and Chungnam National University

detail.title: Segmentation-Guided Quantitative Evaluation of CNN Explanation Fidelity on Out-of-Distribution Chest X-Rays
detail.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy in chest X-ray (CXR) classification tasks. However, their black box nature hinders clinical adoption. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, including Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), generate saliency masks intended to identify the image regions that influence a prediction. However, evaluating quantitatively the anatomical fidelity of these explanations remains a problem to be resolved. We propose a framework for evaluating segmentation that uses the Jaccard Index (Intersection over Union, IoU) to measure the spatial overlap between LIME explanation masks and U-Net-derived lung segmentation masks. These masks are also used in an out-of-distribution (OOD) context where CNNs are trained on images of only the lung (ROI-cropped) and then tested on full CXRs. Experiments on three CNN architectures, AlexNet, VGG16 and VGG19, were tested using 662-image public CXR dataset across two LIME segmentation strategies (superpixel and grid). Based on the results, we can demonstrate that OOD images with $K=30$ in VGG19 achieved a mean IoU of 0.974, VGG16 0.953 and AlexNet achieved 0.862.

title: Power, Participation, and the Limits of Neutrality: Rethinking Court-Annexed Mediation through Ubuntu and Restorative Justice
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Power, Participation, and the Limits of Neutrality: Rethinking Court-Annexed Mediation through Ubuntu and Restorative Justice
detail.abstract: Court-annexed mediation has been increasingly positioned as a corrective to the limitations of adversarial litigation within South Africa's civil justice system, particularly in relation to cost, delay, and procedural rigidity. The assumption that mediation necessarily produces fair and equitable outcomes remains insufficiently interrogated. This article advances a critical examination of the Gauteng Mediation Protocol (GMP) through the lens of power, arguing that mediation does not occur within a neutral social vacuum but is shaped by asymmetries that influence both process and outcome. Drawing on an interpretive qualitative synthesis of socio-legal scholarship, mediation theory, and African philosophical literature, the article contends that while the GMP incorporates elements of restorative justice and ubuntu, it does not adequately confront the embedded power differentials that structure participation in mediation. Rather than dismissing mediation's potential, the analysis situates it within a contested terrain where normative aspirations toward dialogue and relational repair are mediated by institutional, epistemic, and socioeconomic constraints. In doing so, the article contributes to debates on alternative dispute resolution, legal pluralism, and transformative justice by foregrounding the question of power as central to any meaningful evaluation of mediation's capacity to deliver equitable justice.

title: The Cost of Holding On: Cognitive, Behavioural, and Organisational Costs of Losing Positions in Institutional Investment Management

detail.title: The Cost of Holding On: Cognitive, Behavioural, and Organisational Costs of Losing Positions in Institutional Investment Management
detail.abstract: The behavioural finance literature has comprehensively documented the disposition effect, namely the tendency of investors to realise gains too readily and to defer the realisation of losses (Shefrin and Statman, 1985; Odean, 1998; Frazzini, 2006). This paper extends the analysis from the financial cost of disposition behaviour to the broader set of costs that losing positions impose on professional investors. It argues that the principal costs are not pecuniary but cognitive, behavioural, and organisational. Drawing on prospect theory (Kahneman and Tversky, 1979; Tversky and Kahneman, 1991), the limited-attention literature (Kahneman, 1973; Hirshleifer and Teoh, 2003), the empirical work of Akepanidtaworn, Di Mascio, Imas and Schmidt (2023) on institutional selling decisions, and the applied behavioural design framework of Schuller, Mousavi, and Gadzinski (2019), the paper proposes a structured, mandate-aware framework for managing losing positions. The framework rests on five principles: acknowledgement of full carrying cost, recognition of personal behavioural patterns, separation of entry and current decisions, structural pre-commitment, and process-based review. The paper also identifies a structural conflict between disciplined loss management and the calendar-driven incentive structures that govern professional asset management. Meaningful improvement requires architectural intervention rather than awareness alone.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether subjective macroeconomic expectations predict equity risk premia in China. Using professional macro forecasts from the Wind database over 2011-2023, we construct a composite macroeconomic expectation index via PLS. We find that the index significantly and positively predicts future equity premia both in-sample and out-ofsample, implying a countercyclical equity premium. The predictive power is robust to a wide range of macro-financial controls and delivers economically meaningful gains in portfolio allocation. Further analysis shows that controlling for forecast errors does not attenuate predictability, and the subjective index largely subsumes the information in realized macro variables, suggesting that it captures forward-looking macroeconomic conditions rather than belief bias. Cross-sectional and long-horizon results reinforce this interpretation.

title: Legal & Policy Reforms Nigeria Must Prioritise to Compete for Global Capital

detail.title: Legal & Policy Reforms Nigeria Must Prioritise to Compete for Global Capital
detail.abstract: Nigeria has enacted several major reforms over the past decadenotably the Investment and Securities Act (ISA) 2025, Companies & Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, Arbitration & Mediation Act 2023, and a first-ever National Investment Policy (2023)-but gaps remain. Multiple agencies (federal ministries, regulators, and states) still overlap, creating uncertainty. For example, telecoms operators warned that unclear jurisdiction (FCCPC vs. NCC) of an ₦300-400 bn airtime-credit market threatened investor confidence 1. Judicial delays and inconsistent rulings further undermine confidence; ICPC warned that "conflicting trial court judgments" erode faith in justice 2. We find Nigeria needs coordinated regulatory reform across four dimensions: inter-agency coordination, predictable rules, efficient courts, and clear implementation plans. Key reforms should include establishing a National Investment Council to harmonize mandates 3 , 4 , publishing draft rules for public scrutiny 5 , 1 Telcos seek urgent regulation to save N400 billion market value https://guardian.ng/business-services/telcos-seek-urgent-regulation-to-save-n400-billion-marketvalue/

detail.title: Structural Accountability In Emerging Markets Decision Infrastructure and Institutional Resilience in the Age of Acceleration

detail.abstract: Emerging markets are undergoing rapid institutional acceleration driven by artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation, infrastructure expansion, industrialisation, financial inclusion reforms, and regulatory modernisation. While these developments create opportunities for economic growth and inclusion, they simultaneously increase exposure to structural fragility. Evidence across sectors indicates that failures in digital transformation, infrastructure reform, and AI deployment are less frequently technological breakdowns and more frequently failures of accountability architecture. This paper argues that these failures reflect a structural accountability deficit; specifically, diffused decision ownership under conditions of acceleration. The paper introduces a Decision Infrastructure perspective for understanding institutional resilience, focusing on how authority, escalation, risk acceptance, decision memory, and defensibility are structured within high-velocity environments. It advances a structural theory of accountability for emerging markets and proposes a framework for aligning institutional architecture with accelerating decision systems.

title: Reducing Fatigue in Industrial Workplaces: A Motorized Chairless Chair Exoskeleton Approach

detail.title: Reducing Fatigue in Industrial Workplaces: A Motorized Chairless Chair Exoskeleton Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest regarding the publication of this paper

detail.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WRMSDs) remain a major challenge in Industry 4.0 workplaces where prolonged standing, squatting, and repetitive sit-to-stand transitions are common. Passive chairless chairs have been introduced to alleviate fatigue, but their reliance on manual locking mechanisms limits adaptability. This paper presents the design and evaluation of a motorized lower-limb exoskeleton-the Chairless Chair-that integrates electric linear actuators with force-sensing-resistors (FSRs) for intent detection. A finite state machine embedded in a custom PCB enables automated transitions between standing, walking, and semi-sitting postures. Structural safety was validated through finite element analysis, with the mild iron frame sustaining user loads up to 100 kg at FoS ≈ 3, and reducing to ≈ 1.8 under worst-case 120 kg loading. Three iterative prototypes demonstrated reproducible sit-to-stand support, progressively improving structural strength, sensing accuracy, and wearability. Preliminary ergonomic assessment with five subjects (𝑛=5) indicated measurable benefits: Borg CR10 scores decreased from 6.2 to 3.8 (≈ 39 % reduction in subjective fatigue), musculoskeletal effort during a 10-minute squatting task was reduced by ≈ 22 %, and task duration increased by ≈ 45 % in semi-sitting postures. Usability scores averaged 72, reflecting good acceptance but highlighting areas for improvement such as device mass and actuator duty cycle. By combining active actuation, posture-based sensing and embedded control, the Chairless Chair advances beyond passive designs and complements semi-active systems. Its reproducibility, low cost, and adaptability position acts as a promising Industry 4.0 solution for reducing fatigue, improving posture, and enhancing productivity in industrial workplaces.

title: Relational Significance and Mattering: A Multicomponent Study toward a Nordic Model of Outreach Youth Work
affiliations: Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Norwegian University of Science and Technology, KORUS Oslo, KORUS Oslo,  KORUS Nord, University of Bergen and Norwegian University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Relational Significance and Mattering: A Multicomponent Study toward a Nordic Model of Outreach Youth Work
detail.abstract:
Outreach work is an established yet conceptually fragmented field, lacking a systematic understanding of its organization, methodologies, and outcomes. To inform the development of youth-friendly services in Norway, this study explores outreach work targeting children and youth (aged 10–25) in vulnerable life situations. An integrated multicomponent design was employed, combining a scoping review of international literature with expert interviews and stakeholder workshops involving practitioners and youth. 
     Findings indicate that outreach encompasses a wide range of practices, from street-based engagement to digital modalities. Across this diversity, a consistent core emerges: relational work as the foundational mechanism. Conceptualized here as fringe work, outreach operates at the margins of formal service systems to establish trust and facilitate adaptive support and processes of change among youth who might otherwise remain unreached. At the same time, the field is characterized by substantial conceptual ambiguity, particularly regarding the distinction between outreach as a primary methodology and as a supplementary follow-up strategy. 
     Existing research documents positive individual and relational outcomes – such as enhanced safety, coping, and life skills – yet evidence of long-term and system-level impact remains limited. This gap appears to be linked to short-term funding structures and governance frameworks that inadequately capture relational processes.
     Drawing on theories of mattering, the discussion highlights how structural conditions (including siloed organization and performance-oriented management) constrain relational practice. A more precise, relation-based definition of outreach work is proposed, alongside recommendations to safeguard its relational core through strengthened representativeness, long-term institutional anchoring, and hybrid models integrating physical and digital outreach.

detail.abstract: NATO has not made a clear case for how its Human Security Approach and Guiding Principles can improve how the Alliance identifies and responds to insecurities, particularly in a collective defence scenario. To aid the development of the Military Contribution to Human Security (MC2HS), this thematic paper explains how human security is a unique method of analysis underpinned by evidence-based principles. Second, it explains how to operationalize human security within civil-miliary cooperation (CIMIC) and other Joint Functions to improve NATO’s understanding of the human environment. Lastly, it argues a human security approach can improve collective defence operations, including by better preventing and responding to the insecurities faced by the civilian population.

title: Decision Infrastructure Architecture for Institutional Defensibility in Real-Time Systems

detail.title: Decision Infrastructure Architecture for Institutional Defensibility in Real-Time Systems

detail.abstract: The exponential acceleration of real-time computational decision systems across telecommunications, critical infrastructure, finance, and public-sector operations has outpaced the institutional mechanisms designed to oversee them. While significant advances have been made in AI risk management, cyber resilience, and zero-trust architectures, these frameworks do not fully resolve the structural misalignment between decision velocity and institutional accountability. This paper introduces Decision Infrastructure Architecture (DIA) as a structural doctrine that organizes authority distribution, escalation thresholds, override controls, and audit continuity within adaptive, high-velocity environments. Drawing on current literature from 2022-2026 across cybersecurity, AI governance, telecommunications resilience, and institutional trust research, the paper identifies the Acceleration-Accountability Gap (AAG) as a systemic exposure risk. It proposes a layered architecture model designed to preserve institutional defensibility, reduce accountability drift, and sustain trust continuity in real-time decision ecosystems. The implications extend across AI-enabled and non-AI environments, offering a framework for boards, regulators, and system architects to operationalize defensible decision systems at scale. The framework reframes accountability as an architectural requirement rather than a post-event obligation, with direct implications for institutional governance, regulatory oversight, and board-level decision assurance.

title: The Last-Mile Paradox: Quantifying the Operational and Economic Cost of Infrastructure Deficits in the Chakan Industrial Corridor

detail.title: The Last-Mile Paradox: Quantifying the Operational and Economic Cost of Infrastructure Deficits in the Chakan Industrial Corridor
detail.abstract: The Chakan Industrial Area in Maharashtra is a critical node in India's manufacturing network, supporting global automotive OEMs and a vast ecosystem of ancillary equipment suppliers. Despite its world-class production capabilities, the region faces severe logistical constraints due to strained last-mile infrastructure. Utilizing longitudinal empirical observation and traffic data across primary access arteries-including the Dehu Road approach and the Talegaon-Chakan axis-this study quantifies the friction introduced by road conditions, unsegregated traffic, and rapid industrial scaling. Furthermore, it examines the economic impact of delayed freight and human capital drain, while evaluating upcoming macro-interventions like the Pune Ring Road project as long-term catalysts for supply chain resilience and regional industrial growth.

title: 越一致越好？内隐–外显安全态度一致性对员工安全绩效与身体健康的影响
affiliations: Soochow University, Soochow University, Soochow University and Soochow University

detail.title: 越一致越好？内隐–外显安全态度一致性对员工安全绩效与身体健康的影响
detail.abstract: 尽管已有研究证明系统2对系统1的主导作用可以增加安全遵守行为，但外显-内隐一致性如何影响行为与结果仍有待探究。本文运用双系统模型与自我决定理论，探讨个体外显与内隐安全态度的一致性对安全行为及工作场所相关结果（受伤和身体不适）的影响，并考察自主动机在其中的调节作用。两项研究发现，自主动机显著正向调节外显与内隐态度的关系，高自主动机个体具有更高的一致性；外显-内隐一致性越高，员工的安全遵守行为越高，受伤率与身体不适越少；追踪研究显示，依靠外显态度对抗内隐倾向仅在短期有效，而一致性的积极效应则具有跨时间的稳定性。

title: The Three-Stage Leapfrog and Micro Effects of China’s Indigenous AI Computing Power Substitution: An Empirical Study Based on DeepSeek V4 and Huawei Ascend Ecosystem

detail.title: The Three-Stage Leapfrog and Micro Effects of China’s Indigenous AI Computing Power Substitution: An Empirical Study Based on DeepSeek V4 and Huawei Ascend Ecosystem
detail.abstract: The release of the DeepSeek V4 model series in April 2026 marks a historic turning point in the process of indigenous substitution of China's AI computing power industry. This paper systematically demonstrates a new development paradigm for China's indigenous computing power, namely "supernode cluster substitution for single-chip performance", constructs a quantified three-stage leapfrog model for computing power substitution with clear economic foundations and applicable boundaries, and verifies the feasibility of commercial deployment of trillion-parameter large models on domestic NPU platforms. Using frontier econometric methods, this paper empirically examines the economic effects of supernode technology and the policy effects of the national "East Data, West Computing" mega-project, and reveals the micro-mechanisms of indigenous computing power substitution through a dual-case comparative analysis. Meanwhile, this paper develops and empirically tests the theoretical framework of "three-stack synergy" among Ascend, HarmonyOS and openEuler, and systematically compares the differences in computing power independence strategies across five countries. On this basis, this The Three-Stage Leapfrog and Micro Effects of China's Indigenous AI Computing Power Substitution 2 paper constructs quantitative observation indicators focusing on the Ascend industrial chain, and proposes a strategic path for China's indigenous computing power to shift from "catching up" to "leading", providing a new analytical framework and decision support for relevant theoretical research and macro policy formulation.

title: Dual Momentum Allocation Between Physical Gold and Bitcoin (Digital Gold)

detail.title: Dual Momentum Allocation Between Physical Gold and Bitcoin (Digital Gold)
detail.abstract: From the trading desk to the portfolio committee, investors face a familiar question: how should alternative stores of value fit into a diversified portfolio? This research explores that question through a systematic dual-momentum framework comparing Bitcoin and physical gold in a rules-based tactical allocation model. Rather than debating ideology, we focus on practical portfolio construction and risk-adjusted returns. The goal is to examine whether "digital gold" can complement its physical counterpart within a disciplined investment process, and whether the distinct behavior of these assets can be used to build a more effective systematic strategy.

title: Ex Machina: financial stability in the age of artificial intelligence
affiliations: Deutsche Bundesbank, , European Central Bank, Financial Research Division and Centre for Studies in Economics and Finance (CSEF)

detail.title: Ex Machina: financial stability in the age of artificial intelligence

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: Does artificial intelligence (AI) pose a threat to financial stability? We study AI investor behavior, specifically Q-learning and large language model (LLM) investors, in a mutual fund redemption problem with economic and strategic uncertainty. Different AI architectures generate systematically different outcomes. Q-learning investors coordinate well but under default risk exhibit excessive redemption that amplifies fragility. LLM investors internalize equilibrium structure but display belief heterogeneity, weakening coordination and predictability. Our findings show that AI architecture is a first-order determinant of financial stability.

title: Economic Uncertainty and the Beta Anomaly in G10 Countries
affiliations: Sabanci University, Sabanci University Graduate School of Management, Sabanci University and

detail.title: Economic Uncertainty and the Beta Anomaly in G10 Countries
detail.abstract: The beta anomaly, whereby low-beta stocks outperform high-beta stocks on a risk-adjusted basis, remains a persistent challenge to the Capital Asset Pricing Model. A recent study by Cao et al. (2025) links this pattern in U.S. equities to a state-dependent leverage-constraint channel, in which subdued ambiguity and risk aversion during low uncertainty periods push constrained investors toward high-beta stocks, inflating their prices and depressing subsequent returns. We test whether this conditional mechanism extends to the G10 economies. After confirming the original U.S. result over a longer horizon, we partition each international market into high-and low-uncertainty regimes using the global EPU index over 1997-2025. Across most G10 markets, the negative relationship between market beta and CAPM alpha weakens or disappears during high-uncertainty periods, but becomes significantly more pronounced when uncertainty is low. The pattern survives alternative specifications of the global index, country-level EPU measures, and different beta estimation methods.

detail.abstract: We test whether the sectoral cross-section heterogeneity of forward equity returns following bank-credit-supply shocks-established for the United States by a companion paper using the Federal Reserve Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS)-generalises internationally. Applying an identical AR(1)-residual shock-identification scheme to the European Central Bank's Bank Lending Survey (ECB BLS) over 94 quarters and the Bank of England's Credit Conditions Survey (BoE CCS) over 76 quarters, we measure forward 1-, 3-, and 6-month cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) on STOXX Europe 600 firms with historical-reconstitution membership (Compustat Global, gvkeyx = 150,376) and apply the same Bonferroni-K=33 celllevel test plus a four-test robustness battery as the US benchmark. At the 6-month horizon the Eurozone sector ranking correlates Spearman rho = +0.755 (p = 0.007) with the US benchmark, strongly meeting our pre-registered rho >= 0.5 external-validation criterion; eight of 33 sector-horizon cells reach Bonferroni significance, the F-test for sector heterogeneity at 6 m is p = 2.7e-10, and three of four robustness tests pass. A complementary long-Industrials / short-{Communications, Utilities} basket delivers an alpha-Sharpe of +2.32 after absorbing a five-block factor baseline. The UK companion analysis fails Bonferroni at the cell level (1 of 33), but ANOVA confirms sector heterogeneity at 1 m and 3 m horizons; we explain this through a pre-registered universe-power lemma-STOXX 600 GBR is a vendor substitute for the unavailable FTSE 350, dominated by multinationals (BP, Shell, GSK, AstraZeneca, HSBC) whose economics are weakly identified by a domestic UK credit-supply shock, with a per-cell sample of n = 50 to 284 implying a structural Bonferroni floor of zero to one cells. This paper is a replication paper, not a novel-finding paper; the mechanism belongs to the companion US paper and the BLS macro literature, and our contribution is replication priority on the precise five-axis intersection (BLS/CCS survey AR(1) shock × STOXX 600 universe × eleven-sector cross-section × Bonferroni-K=33 multiple-comparison correction × medium-horizon forward CAR).

title:
FQ-SHAP: Fuzzy Logic Enhanced Explainability for Quantum Circuits 
An Extension of Q-SHAP via Fuzzy Gate Classification, Importance-Weighted Consistency, and Entanglement-Aware Pruning

detail.title:
FQ-SHAP: Fuzzy Logic Enhanced Explainability for Quantum Circuits 
An Extension of Q-SHAP via Fuzzy Gate Classification, Importance-Weighted Consistency, and Entanglement-Aware Pruning
detail.abstract: We present FQ-SHAP (Fuzzy Q-SHAP), a novel extension of the Q-SHAP framework that integrates fuzzy logic into quantum circuit explainability. Classical explainability metrics treat gate importance as crisp values, collapsing the rich graded structure of quantum information flow into hard thresholds and equally penalizing all explanation discrepancies regardless of the gates' semantic significance. FQ-SHAP introduces five complementary contributions: (1) fuzzy gate importance classification using triangular membership functions over four linguistic labels (negligible, minor, moderate, critical); (2) an importance-weighted fuzzy consistency metric that down-weights disagreements on negligible gates; (3) a Mamdani fuzzy inference system (FIS) for entanglement-aware gate pruning; (4) fuzzy qubit role classification; and (5) linguistic explanation generation with hedgequalified natural language per gate. Evaluated on five benchmark quantum circuits Bell State, GHZ (3-qubit), Grover's search (2-qubit), hardware-efficient VQE ansätz, and quantum teleportation FQ-SHAP identifies all entanglement-creating gates correctly as keep with 100% accuracy, recommends pruning 62% of gates overall, and produces membership heatmaps that expose graded importance structure invisible to crisp Q-SHAP scores. Consistency scores range from 0.600 to 0.845, peaking in parameterized circuits with low entanglement. The fuzzy pruning FIS correctly overrides fidelityonly decisions in the hardware-efficient ansätz, where the CNOT gate carries lower fidelity importance than rotation gates yet remains physically indispensable.

detail.abstract: This study utilizes unique data on the network of farmers who are members of autonomous micro-credit groups combined with randomized control trials, to investigate the effects of social network and self-learning on the long-term adoption of crop insurance. Premium subsidies were randomly assigned to 729 farmers across 44 Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) in Lai Chau province of Vietnam over three rice cropping seasons. Each farmer's network was defined by the five fellow VSLA members with whom they most frequently discussed agricultural production and financial matters. The results showed that, in the first season when crop insurance was introduced for the first time, there was evidence of conformity or imitation among farmers. However, the effect was only short-lived and diminished in the subsequent rice cropping seasons. Importantly, we found substantially positive effect of experiencing insurance payouts on the uptake. Not only did receiving their own payouts but also observing others' payouts in the farmer network increase their future uptake. This effect was driven by the improved insurance knowledge, updated risk perception and greater trust in the insurance provider, which highlighted the roles of social learning and personal experience. Our findings indicated that the mechanisms of the existence of network effects changed over time from conformity to social learning across multiple rice cropping seasons.

title: Informality and Patronalism in Argentina: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Role of Informality and Patronalism in Regime Paradigms

detail.title: Informality and Patronalism in Argentina: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Role of Informality and Patronalism in Regime Paradigms
detail.abstract: Argentina presents a distinctive puzzle in the comparative study of patronal politics. Throughout the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, Argentina has oscillated repeatedly between liberal-democratic and patronal regimes, unable to stabilize in either direction. This study applies the conceptual framework of "The Anatomy of Post-Communist Regimes" to analyze Argentina's political evolution from colonial patronalism through independence, the exceptional Liberal Republic (1853-1930), and the subsequent cycles of military and civilian patronal rule. Using the Unified Theory Matrix (UTM) to classify regimes across five dimensions of formal political domination and five modes of collusions between the social spheres of politics and economy, I identify Argentina's dominant pattern as "oscillating patronalism"a structural tendency to alternate between different regime types without achieving stable consolidation. The analysis reveals how weak institutional foundations, combined with recurring economic crises and military intervention, create conditions for this patronal oscillation. Argentina's case contributes to the Political Capitalisms project by demonstrating the Anatomy's framework's applicability to Latin American contexts and by theorizing a distinct form of patronal instability that differs from more linear trajectories.

title: Property regimes under planetary crisis: strategic rationality and ecological embeddedness

detail.title: Property regimes under planetary crisis: strategic rationality and ecological embeddedness

detail.abstract: This paper examines how planetary ecological limits alter the strategic role of property regimes within contemporary legal orders. Drawing on ecological economics and critical property theory, it argues that dominant corporate ownership structures facilitate the externalisation of social and ecological costs, thereby contributing to systemic instability under conditions of ecological constraints. When the economy is understood as embedded within a finite biosphere, property arrangements cannot be treated as neutral distributive mechanisms, but instead function as strategic infrastructure, shaping incentives, risk allocation, and long-term governance stability. The paper further suggests that this is not only a question of institutional design, but of epistemology. Dominant property frameworks render ecological relations and environmental harm only partially visible, insofar as they are recognised primarily through categories of economic value or legally cognisable injury. The paper argues that plural and stewardship-oriented property forms may enhance resilience under crisis conditions and situates legal reform within broader debates on socio-ecological transformation.

title: Informality and Patronalism in Venezuela: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Role of Informality and Patronalism in Regime Paradigms

detail.title: Informality and Patronalism in Venezuela: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Role of Informality and Patronalism in Regime Paradigms
detail.abstract: This study explores the evolution of patronalism as a structural and cultural pattern shaping Venezuelan political and social development. By tracing the oscillation between institutional and informal modes of power, it reveals how clientelist and rent-based dependencies have persisted beneath shifting ideological and regime paradigms. The analysis connects economic cycles, state formation, and societal transformation to demonstrate how informality functions not as an exception, but as a constitutive logic of governance. Drawing on comparative insights, the work positions Venezuelan history as a paradigmatic case of patronal continuity under changing political forms. It offers a theoretical sketch and a conceptual framework for understanding the role of informality in regime dynamics across time.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether large language models (LLMs), grounded in theory and calibrated against empirical data, can approximate aggregate firm behaviour. The analysis focuses on innovative activity, as measured by the Community Innovation Survey (CIS). Using structured natural-language profiles of German firms, we compare an uncalibrated baseline with two calibrated variants that combine theory grounding with empirical anchoring through firm-specific web-derived indicators and patent data, differing only in how theory weights are optimised. The uncalibrated baseline largely over-predicts innovation. Both calibrated variants substantially improve accuracy and align predictions with observed cross-industry patterns, in a validation that is both temporally displaced and calibrated using independent cross-source information. Theory-level prediction patterns broadly align with patterns expected from innovation and management literature. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed framework for LLM-based firm simulation, opening avenues for further work leveraging synthetic firms for experimentation or counterfactual analysis on organisational behaviour.

title: Complex Doesn't Mean Complicated-and Why it Matters for Political Economy

detail.title: Complex Doesn't Mean Complicated-and Why it Matters for Political Economy
detail.abstract: Yuen Yuen Ang introduces Adaptive Political Economy (APE), a paradigm that reconceptualizes political economies as complex adaptive systems rather than complicated, machine-like objects. Drawing on Benoit Mandelbrot's fractal mathematics as a meta-analogy, Ang argues that modern social science operates under an inherited "industrial paradigm" that reduces nonlinear social realities to linear cause-and-effect models. Using China's post-1980s transformation as a primary demonstration case, Ang maps development as a three-step coevolutionary process: normatively weak institutions build new markets, emerging markets stimulate stronger institutions, and stronger institutions preserve those markets. Ang situates APE as one pillar of a broader framework she terms AIM—Adaptive, Inclusive, and Moral Political Economy—which challenges the assumption that Western institutional arrangements represent a universal developmental endpoint and, drawing on Edward Said's Orientalism, foregrounds how power and positionality shape knowledge production in the social sciences.

title: Hidden Costs of Sustainability: Household labor and the Political Economy of Environmental Policy (Working Paper)

detail.title: Hidden Costs of Sustainability: Household labor and the Political Economy of Environmental Policy (Working Paper)
detail.abstract:
This paper examines how sustainability policies are implemented within households and investigates the distribution of labor required to sustain environmentally aligned practices. It argues that the implementation of sustainability policies is a labor-mediated process, structured by intra-household inequalities and shaped by gender and migration. 

Using Australia as a policy-rich case study, the paper adopts an interpretive, theory-guided secondary analysis. It integrates quantitative evidence (such as time-use and labor data), policy analysis (energy and waste) and interdisciplinary scholarship on gender, migration and household practices. This approach examines how environmental expectations are translated into everyday domestic life. 

The findings demonstrate that such policy implementations are not frictionless but depend on sustained cognitive, emotional and organisational efforts within households. This labor, conceptualised as environmental emotional labor, is unevenly distributed, disproportionately borne by women. It is further intensified in migrant households where policy expectations must be interpreted across cultural and institutional contexts. As a result, sustainability policies generate hidden distributional effects by externalising implementation costs into unpaid domestic labor. In doing so, the paper frames sustainability policy as a political economy process in which costs are redistributed rather than eliminated. 

This paper's originality lies in reframing household sustainability as a labor-intensive process and introducing the concept of Household Policy Burden(HPB) to capture time, cognitive and coordination demands associated with compliance. By making these hidden inputs visible, the study contributes to a more realistic and equitable understanding of environmental policy design and evaluation.

title: Changes in Mindfulness, Empathy, Self-Leadership, and Clinical Competence Following an Empathy-Based Nursing Leadership Class in Nursing Students

detail.title: Changes in Mindfulness, Empathy, Self-Leadership, and Clinical Competence Following an Empathy-Based Nursing Leadership Class in Nursing Students
detail.abstract: Background and Aim: Empathy is recognized as a core component of nursing leadership; however, limited research has investigated the impact of empathy-based leadership education on nursing students’ psychological and clinical competencies. This study evaluated changes in mindfulness, empathy, self-leadership, and clinical competence among nursing students following participation in an empathy-based nursing leadership class.Methods: This study used a one group pretest–posttest design. Seventy-three third-year nursing students participated in an eight-week empathy-based nursing leadership class at a university in Korea during the first semester of 2025. The program integrated empathy-centered nursing leadership content with mindfulness-based training to promote empathic engagement and emotion regulation. Students engaged in reflective journaling and group projects designed to apply leadership skills in practice. Self-reported measures of mindfulness, empathy, self-leadership, and clinical competence were collected before and after the course. Paired t-tests were used to analyze data to examine pre- and post-intervention differences in study variables.Results: Positive correlations were observed among mindfulness, empathy, self-leadership, and clinical competence, showing that higher levels of mindfulness and empathy were associated with greater self-leadership and clinical competence. Participation in the empathy-based nursing leadership class resulted in significant increases in mindfulness, empathy, self-, and clinical competence.Conclusions: The empathy-based nursing leadership class was associated with improvements in students’ emotional and professional competencies, supporting the integration of empathy-centered and mindfulness-based approaches into leadership education. This evidence suggests that fostering mindfulness and empathy may strengthen nursing students’ self-leadership and clinical competence, eventually contributing to more compassionate and patient-centered care.

title: Krushi Guide: An AI-Enabled Smart Farming Assistant for Sustainable Smallholder Agriculture

detail.title: Krushi Guide: An AI-Enabled Smart Farming Assistant for Sustainable Smallholder Agriculture
detail.abstract: Agriculture is a critical source of income for millions of people globally, especially in developing countries where the majority of farmers own and work on small plots of land. Despite its importance to these communities, smallholder farmers face numerous ongoing challenges, including crop diseases, unstable weather patterns, fluctuating market prices, and a lack of access to timely agricultural advice. All of these factors often lead to decreased productivity, financial uncertainty, and increased uncertainty about farming decisions. Additionally, many farmers do not have access to effective technology-based advisory services or modern agricultural tools, thus revealing an urgent need for simple, inclusive digital solutions that can enable sustainable agricultural development and food security. Krushi Guide is a smart digital farming assistant designed to help smallholder farmers with their daily farming activities. Krushi is a mobile and web-based platform that incorporates state-of-the-art technologies to deliver timely, practical assistance to farmers as they work on their farms. The platform's primary features include artificial intelligence-assisted detection of crop diseases via image capture, localized

title: "Turning Polycrisis into Polytunity." Keynote Speech at the DSA Conference (27 June 2025)

detail.title: "Turning Polycrisis into Polytunity." Keynote Speech at the DSA Conference (27 June 2025)
detail.abstract: Yuen Yuen Ang challenges the Western-centric framing of the "polycrisis" — arguing that the term, popularized by elite institutions like the World Economic Forum, names fear without diagnosing its structural causes or acknowledging the long history of crises endured by the Global Majority. In its place, Ang proposes polytunity: a generational opening to rethink not only institutions but the paradigms undergirding development scholarship itself. Ang traces today's overlapping crises to the industrial-colonial paradigm — a worldview combining mechanical, reductionist thinking with the assumption that Western institutions represent the universal endpoint of development. As an alternative, she presents AIM — Adaptive, Inclusive, and Moral Political Economy — which replaces machine thinking with systems thinking, Western templates with indigenous innovation, and false objectivity with transparency about how power shapes knowledge. Drawing on her books How China Escaped the Poverty Trap (2016) and China's Gilded Age (2020), Ang demonstrates AIM as both method and compass for development scholars navigating a disrupted, multipolar world.

title: Audit Pulse: A Smart Digital Assistant for Prompt Engineered Financial Oversight

detail.title: Audit Pulse: A Smart Digital Assistant for Prompt Engineered Financial Oversight
detail.abstract: Modern enterprises generate financial data at a pace that has fundamentally outrun the audit methods built to govern it. Traditional auditing relies on samplinga practical compromise that leaves the vast majority of transactions unexamined and, consequently, leaves organizations exposed to fraud and compliance failures that go undetected for months. AuditPulse is a smart digital framework that confronts this problem head-on by replacing manual sampling with full-population analysis driven by prompt-engineered artificial intelligence. The framework addresses two long-standing weaknesses in current practice: the structural blind spot created by sampling, and the profession's near-total neglect of unstructured data-contracts, emails, internal memos-which often carry the most revealing evidence of misconduct. Through a Cognitive Orchestration Layer, a Semantic Interrogation module, Full-Population Triangulation, and a Recursive Review Loop that mandates verifiable citations for every AI-generated finding, AuditPulse enables auditors to examine 100% of their data with a reliability and traceability that purely manual methods cannot achieve.
