title: Men for Makeup: Rise of Men in Fashion and Makeup Industry and Backlash in Digital Media

detail.title: Men for Makeup: Rise of Men in Fashion and Makeup Industry and Backlash in Digital Media
detail.abstract: Today, the beauty industry is becoming more inclusive. In fact, the personal care market for men is projected to hit $276.9 billion by 2030. These changing trends and the growing market potential have redefined the cosmetics industry's approach, making beauty no longer just a woman's affair. Media has a profound role in shaping societal norms and perceptions of masculinity, as there is a growing trend towards more diverse and inclusive representations. By challenging traditional notions and showcasing alternative masculinities, media can play a pivotal role in promoting a more equitable and understanding society. This paper takes an attempt to analyse the growing representation of men in fashion and makeup industry by breaking traditional gender norms, interpret the hate and backlash faced by them in digital media and review the perception of individuals upon men deviating from traditional idea of masculinity. This research follows a methodology of content analysis, involving social media analysis and online questionnaire to understand the opinion of people about redefining masculinity. The samples were collected through purposive sampling for selectively analysing the content of media influencers and snowball sampling for getting opinion from 18-25 aged men and women. Thus, the intersection of Gender, Fashion and Media is studied through symbolic interactionism theory.

title: From "Experience-Driven" to "Data-Driven": A Paradigm Shift in Safety Governance for High-Risk Industries --A BAM-Based Systematic Diagnosis of the "5•4" Huasheng Fireworks Explosion in Liuyang

detail.title: From "Experience-Driven" to "Data-Driven": A Paradigm Shift in Safety Governance for High-Risk Industries --A BAM-Based Systematic Diagnosis of the "5•4" Huasheng Fireworks Explosion in Liuyang
detail.abstract: On May 4, 2026, an explosion occurred at the Huasheng Fireworks Manufacturing Company in Liuyang, Hunan Province, resulting in 26 fatalities and 61 injuries (as of press time on May 7). This was not an isolated accident but a foreseeable consequence of the systemic failure of the "experience-driven" safety governance model. Based on the BAM (Behavior Amplification Model), this paper conducts an immediate diagnosis within 72 hours of the accident: the S-value drifted from "safety first" to "meeting production deadlines"; the E-value (risk concern transmission efficiency) fractured during repeated inspections; the M-value failed to claim safety responsibility due to a "fines-over-management" approach; the I-value (inhibitory factor) showed no response to minimal fines (P = 1-I, with P ≈ 0.95 when I ≈ 0.05); and the A-value (closed-loop verification) completely idled as corrective actions became mere formalities. This paper proposes a four-level transformation framework for "data-driven" safety governance in high-risk industries: full-parameter monitoring at the enterprise level, AI-based intelligent inspection at the industry level, A-value closed-loop governance at the regulatory level, and long-term mechanisms at the institutional level. The BAM diagnosis concludes with a core assertion: it is not that the people are broken, but that the parameters are broken; and it is not that controls are insufficient, but that the mode of control is flawed.

title: La gestion des ruptures amoureuses au travail dans un contexte québécois
affiliations: University of Quebec at Rimouski - Department of Management Sciences and University of Quebec at Rimouski - Department of Management Sciences

detail.title: La gestion des ruptures amoureuses au travail dans un contexte québécois
detail.abstract:
Romantic relationships in the workplace are a foreseeable outcome in environments where men and women regularly interact. This phenomenon has become increasingly common as gender parity progresses in Canadian and Quebec workplaces over the past 30 years. Romantic relationships may sometimes come to an end, resulting in a breakup, with reasonably expected consequences, including conflicts that can negatively impact the work climate for both former partners and their colleagues.

The primary aim of this study is to identify, describe, and analyse practices and strategies that employers and managers could adopt to manage romantic breakups within the workplace that have negative consequences on the work climate and both individual and collective performance. To conduct this research, semi-structured interviews were held with seven employees working in Quebec.
The results reveal two key insights. Firstly, workplace romances are accepted as a reality, along with the breakups and their negative effects on individuals and the work environment. Secondly, organisations and managers in Québec need to take action rather than remain inactive, fostering a healthy work climate while respecting employees' privacy. Seven organisational measures were evaluated, with participants either fully or partially receptive to them, providing potential solutions for managing workplace breakups.
This research contributes to scientific knowledge by examining an almost inevitable yet scarcely studied reality in Québec, Francophone communities, and Canada: managing romantic breakups in the workplace. The findings offer organisations and managers relevant approaches and organisational measures to support a healthy work environment and to assist employees in navigating the emotional challenges of a breakup. Consequently, these measures will help organisations better fulfil their legal obligation in Québec to ensure a healthy, harassment-free workplace, and will also support employee retention.
Keywords: breakup, romance, work climate, workplace, perception, guidance, management, harassment, couple, accommodation

title: The Anatomy of Atrocity: A Century of Human Rights Violations in Sudan (2003-2025)

detail.title: The Anatomy of Atrocity: A Century of Human Rights Violations in Sudan (2003-2025)
detail.abstract: The paper examines the continuum of mass human rights violations in Sudan from the Darfur genocide (2003-2005) through the ongoing civil war (2023-2025). Drawing on reports from the United Nations, the International Criminal Court, Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, and the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), the analysis traces how a state-building failure and the institutionalization of militia violence produced cycles of atrocity crimes. The paper documents that between 2003 and 2008, approximately 300,000 civilians died in Darfur, with 2.7 million displaced. From April 2023 to December 2025, the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has killed over 40,000 people, displaced 14 million, and pushed 21.2 million people (45% of the population) into acute food insecurity, with famine confirmed in multiple locations. The paper argues that the RSF, as the direct successor to the Janjaweed, has operationalized genocide as a systematic tool of territorial control, while the SAF has committed war crimes through indiscriminate bombardment and the recruitment of child soldiers. International responses, including UN sanctions and ICC prosecutions, have proven insufficient to deter ongoing atrocities. The paper concludes that accountability mechanisms require urgent reform to address the structural impunity that has enabled successive Sudanese regimes to weaponize ethnic violence.

title: Understanding Fertility Today: Young Couples' Expectations about the Consequences of Childbearing
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology - School of Economics and Dongbei University of Finance & Economics

detail.title: Understanding Fertility Today: Young Couples' Expectations about the Consequences of Childbearing
detail.abstract: Fertility decisions are forward-looking and made within couples, yet little is known about how young couples perceive the consequences of childbearing. We survey 1,800 respondents from paired Chinese one-child couples and elicit second-birth plans and expectations about life outcomes under alternative fertility choices, including consumption, wages, time burdens, and old-age support. We use these data to estimate a household bargaining model. Wives are more likely than husbands to oppose a second birth. The main driver of this disagreement is not wives' weak bargaining power, but gender differences in preferences over child quantity. Policy simulations show that public childcare, especially when it also reduces motherhood wage penalties, is more effective than cash transfers. The old-age value of children operates more through support in adverse health states than through financial transfers, but an additional child provides only limited extra insurance. These results show the value of measuring the beliefs and trade-offs that shape fertility decisions among current cohorts.

title: A Decomposition of Experiential Utility: Pain Relief and Comfort

detail.title: A Decomposition of Experiential Utility: Pain Relief and Comfort
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a decomposition of experiential utility into two distinct components: Pain-Relief Utility and Comfort Utility. While existing frameworks treat improvements in lived experience as arising from a single process, the analysis here argues that the alleviation of negative states and the enhancement of positive conditions operate through fundamentally different psychological and behavioral mechanisms. Pain-relief processes are characterized by high salience, urgency, and constraint removal, reflecting the need to restore basic functioning in the presence of deprivation. In contrast, comfort-enhancing processes are more gradual and diffuse, improving quality of life beyond baseline sufficiency. 

Building on the Wealth Utility Continuum, the paper formalizes this distinction by expressing experiential utility as the sum of pain-relief and comfort components. A graphical representation illustrates how the composition of experiential utility evolves across the wealth distribution, with pain-relief mechanisms dominating at low levels of wealth and comfort mechanisms becoming increasingly important as basic needs are secured. 

This decomposition provides a mechanism-based interpretation of diminishing returns in experiential well-being. Rather than arising solely from curvature in a single utility function, diminishing returns reflect a shift in the underlying sources of utility-from the alleviation of deprivation to the enhancement of comfort. The framework offers a psychologically grounded and economically interpretable approach to understanding how wealth shapes lived experience.

title: The AI Circular Economy: Systemic Risk, Vendor Financing, and the Keystone Problem

detail.title: The AI Circular Economy: Systemic Risk, Vendor Financing, and the Keystone Problem
detail.abstract: This paper identifies and maps a structural phenomenon in the artificial intelligence industry: a self-reinforcing system of circular financing in which the same pool of capital rotates continuously among a small group of companies, principally Nvidia, OpenAI, Microsoft, Oracle, AMD, CoreWeave, SoftBank, and xAI, creating the appearance of robust revenue growth, soaring valuations, and unprecedented infrastructure demand. We identify seven distinct circular financing loops, totalling over $1.4 trillion in committed future spending, and demonstrate that OpenAI occupies the keystone position in this system: the single entity whose insolvency would simultaneously impair the demand assumptions, revenue projections, and collateral valuations of every other participant. We draw structural comparisons to three historical episodes, the 2000-2002 telecom equipment collapse (vendor financing), the 2007-2009 Lehman Brothers crisis (counterparty opacity and off-balance-sheet leverage), and the 2014-2016 oil price crash (physical overbuilding with subsequent commodity price collapse), and argue that the AI circular economy combines pathologies from all three. We further identify ten systemic questions that remain unanswered, outline a plausible 12-18 month cascade timeline, and assess Oracle, CoreWeave, and Nvidia as the three weakest secondary nodes. The paper concludes that the AI infrastructure buildout, at approximately $650-700 billion in projected 2026 capital expenditure, represents the largest single-sector debt-financed construction programme in modern economic history, and that the gap between committed infrastructure spending and realised end-user revenue, estimated at $800 billion annually by 2030 (Bain & Company, 2025), constitutes a systemic risk that has not been adequately priced by financial markets.

title: Programmable Repayment: Risk-Sharing and Enforcement Through the Payment Platform
affiliations: University of Lausanne - Faculty of Business and Economics (HEC Lausanne) and University of Bern

detail.title: Programmable Repayment: Risk-Sharing and Enforcement Through the Payment Platform
detail.abstract: Payment platforms increasingly originate credit and recover it by withholding a share of each merchant sale at settlement. We call this contract programmable repayment (PR). PR is state-contingent debt on platform-recorded sales. It transfers part of the merchant's cash-flow risk to the lender and automates collection, but the merchant chooses which sales are processed through the platform. This puts the contract's risksharing benefit in tension with its enforcement reach. At an Indian payment fintech running PR at scale, merchants with more volatile sales and outside-credit pressure accept offers more often. After disbursal, high-volatility merchants drive the platformsales decline relative to matched controls. The same merchant diverts substantially more on her second loan than her first, learning to substitute toward digital channels where cash becomes scarce. The contract's pledgeability is therefore endogenous to borrower experience. The lender nevertheless earns positive returns: high-volatility merchants default less and stay longer on the platform.

title: Retrenchment Signaling and the Erosion of NATO Credibility under Trump 2.0
affiliations: Charles University , , Charles University in Prague, Charles University in Prague and Charles University

detail.title: Retrenchment Signaling and the Erosion of NATO Credibility under Trump 2.0
detail.abstract: Has Trump’s confrontational stance toward U.S. allies undermined NATO’s credibility? To address this critical question, we conducted a large, survey-based longitudinal study investigating changes in perceptions of NATO’s collective defense commitments across selected allied states (the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, and Canada), the Russian Federation, and in the British and German parliaments. In line with our theory of retrenchment signaling, we found a dramatic decline in the credibility of the U.S. commitments to NATO during the first year of Trump’s second administration (first-order effect), accompanied by a more modest increase in the credibility of non-U.S. allies (second-order effect). We demonstrate that the net impact on NATO’s overall credibility has been negative, showing asymmetric alliances suffer from a “substitution deficit” in credibility signaling. Furthermore, our investigation in Russia suggests that U.S. retrenchment signaling has even more negative consequences for allied deterrence than assurance due to the “strongest-link bias,” in which adversaries tend to overidentify the credibility of asymmetric alliances with that of their leading power. Finally, we show that political elites across allied states have been at least as skeptical about the U.S. commitment to defend its allies as the general population. Our longitudinal study provides the first systematic empirical evidence of the erosion of NATO’s credibility under “Trump 2.0” and contributes to scholarship on the dynamics of military alliances and the impact of great power retrenchment on world politics.

title: An Empirical Assessment on Bank Competition and Efficiency in Nepal

detail.title: An Empirical Assessment on Bank Competition and Efficiency in Nepal
detail.abstract:
Background: Nepalese banking sector has undergone significant structural changes following financial liberalization and recent consolidation policies. However, there is limited empirical evidence on interaction between bank competition and efficiency. 

Objectives: This study examines the relationship between competition and efficiency in Nepalese commercial banks and evaluates their short run and long run dynamics. 

Data and Methodology: Using bank level panel data from 2011-2023, competition is measured by Lerner Index and efficiency by Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA). Panel co-integration tests assess long run relationships while Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) captures adjustment dynamics. 

Results: The findings indicate competitive banking environment in Nepal with moderate efficiency levels. Co-integration confirm stable long run relationship between competition and efficiency. VECM estimates reveal bidirectional adjustment, with efficiency responding faster to disequilibrium than competition. 

Conclusions: Competition and efficiency are interdependent in the long run. Policies to promote these aspects can strengthen performance of Nepalese banking sector and financial stability.

title: Ternary Logic as Constitutional Substrate: A Triadic Computational Governance Architecture for High-Stakes Automated Decision-Making

detail.title: Ternary Logic as Constitutional Substrate: A Triadic Computational Governance Architecture for High-Stakes Automated Decision-Making
detail.abstract: This report analyzes Ternary Logic (TL) as a comprehensive computational governance architecture for high-stakes automated decision-making systems, evaluating its capacity to operate across software, hardware, and institutional layers. The foundational innovation—the Epistemic Hold (0) state—enables structured uncertainty management through formal computational hesitation, physically realized via Delay Insensitive Ternary Logic (DITL) hardware. Drawing on technical documentation from the TernaryLogic framework, peer-reviewed DITL circuit research, and hardware implementation studies, this analysis assesses whether native triadic computational architectures (+1, 0, −1) can serve as enforceable governance mechanisms for financial infrastructure, supply chain verification, regulatory compliance automation, and advanced artificial intelligence systems. The evaluation encompasses semiconductor feasibility, formal verification methodologies, failure mode analysis, and comparative assessment against alternative governance approaches including blockchain systems, trusted execution environments, and pure software governance. Key findings indicate that TL's hardware-enforced hesitation, combined with tri-cameral institutional oversight and immutable evidentiary architectures, yields a constitutional substrate robust under recursive self-improvement and decentralized intelligence scenarios.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Resource Orchestration in SDN-Enabled Fog-Edge Computing: A Lyapunov-Guided Primal-Dual Framework
affiliations: National University Singapore, University of Tokyo, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) - Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Students and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Resource Orchestration in SDN-Enabled Fog-Edge Computing: A Lyapunov-Guided Primal-Dual Framework
detail.abstract: The convergence of software-defined networking (SDN) with fog-edge computing has unlocked unprecedented opportunities for ultra-low-latency distributed intelligence. However, existing resource orchestration mechanisms suffer from three fundamental limitations: (i) centralized decision-making that collapses under large-scale heterogeneity, (ii) myopic optimization of latency-energy tradeoffs without hard quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees, and (iii) vulnerability to node failures and dynamic workload bursts. This paper introduces HiDRL-Edge-a hierarchical multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework that achieves scalable, resilient, and QoS-aware resource orchestration in SDN-enabled fog-edge networks. Our contributions are fourfold. First, we formulate a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) with chance constraints for tail latency and reliability, transforming it into a primal-dual optimization with learnable Lagrange multipliers. Second, we propose a graph neural network (GNN) embedding layer that captures spatial-temporal dependencies across heterogeneous edge nodes, enabling sample-efficient multi-agent coordination via central.

title: Regional Growth Associated with SEZs, Socio-Economic and Spatial Imbalances: Impact of Corporate Agglomeration and FDI in Gabon's Forestry Sector and Proposal of a Sustainable Governance Model (DGMUG) Applicable to Southern Countries

detail.title: Regional Growth Associated with SEZs, Socio-Economic and Spatial Imbalances: Impact of Corporate Agglomeration and FDI in Gabon's Forestry Sector and Proposal of a Sustainable Governance Model (DGMUG) Applicable to Southern Countries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declares that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

keywords: planning and dynamic management of imbalances Development clusters
planning and dynamic management of imbalances

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of firm agglomeration on foreign direct investment (FDI), public investment, export revenues, and industrial income in Gabon's forestry sector, comparing the Nkok Special Economic Zone (SEZ) with areas outside the SEZ. Using robust econometric approaches-including ordinary least squares (OLS) time-series and bias-corrected (BC) panel models-the analysis highlights socioeconomic and geographic disparities within Gabon's forestry industry. The study also assesses the effects of FDI and public investment on firm clustering, exports, and industrial income in both zones. Following an evaluation of disparities in Gabon's forestry sector, the study proposes a Dynamic Governance Model for Uneven Growth (DGMUG) to manage accelerated development and mitigate resulting inequalities. The findings reveal that the Nkok SEZ benefits from favorable industrialization conditions, marked by strong growth, sustained exports, and concentrated FDI supported by public investment. In contrast, peripheral regions experience slower and less stable growth due to structural challenges and insufficient targeted investments. Furthermore, while FDI combined with public investment has a positive impact in Nkok, it exerts a negative effect outside the SEZ, exacerbating geographic polarization. Post-2018, investments in the SEZ declined, likely due to market saturation and weakened public-private cooperation, whereas investments outside the SEZ remained limited. To address these imbalances, the study introduces the DGMUG as a complementary framework to existing strategies, such as those of the World Bank (2011). This model outlines three phases: (1) initial polarization, (2) an acceleration phase with potential scenarios (lethal, stagnation, or acceleration-diversification), and (3) a transition toward regional equilibrium. The study underscores the mechanisms of polarization and resulting inequalities while proposing strategies to mitigate disparities and foster more balanced regional development.

title: The Backbone Pattern: A Graph-Substrate Architecture for Governing Multi-Agent AI Ecosystems

detail.title: The Backbone Pattern: A Graph-Substrate Architecture for Governing Multi-Agent AI Ecosystems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This research was conducted independently.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Multi-agent AI ecosystems-organizations running multiple autonomous AI agents that take real actions, delegate tasks to each other, and operate under human-issued mandates-are fundamentally relational: the entities that compose them (agents, mandates, domains, artifacts) matter less in isolation than in how they connect-who delegates to whom, what authorization scopes which action, which test traces to which requirement, how one domain trusts another. The apparent conclusion, that a graph database should therefore hold the entirety of agentic state, is the trap. This article proposes the Backbone Pattern: a graph substrate is the coordination layer of the ecosystem-the canonical map of topology, mandates, and traceability-and nothing more. Enforcement runs at the agent edge from compiled policy artifacts (small, fast rulesets derived from the graph) with continuous round-trip validation (ongoing checks that the compiled rules still match the graph). Large payloads live in object storage, referenced by lightweight anchor nodes (graph nodes that index external data rather than containing it) under a strict binding discipline. Revocation is bounded-meaning deliberately governed by an explicit time window-rather than pretended to be instant, which is physically impossible in distributed systems.

This paper is also available on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19774002

title: How to Measure Market Risk on Crypto Markets

detail.title: How to Measure Market Risk on Crypto Markets
detail.abstract: The paper presents the challenges in crypto trading and introduces an approach to solve the open issues. The solution is a free toolkit available free on https://analysis-tool-4oln.onrender.com/. It derives risk signals by calibrating Levy Process to crypto returns, applies Fractional Fokker-Planck Equation to marker information, and leverages WGAN-GP.

title: Transformation of the Money Supply Structure and Formation of Sources of "Long Money" in the Russian Economy: Problems and Prospects

detail.title: Transformation of the Money Supply Structure and Formation of Sources of "Long Money" in the Russian Economy: Problems and Prospects

keywords: sovereign wealth funds JEL Classification: E41

detail.abstract: Purpose. This article analyzes the transformation of Russia's money supply structure and identifies the key challenges in forming long-term financial resources ("long money") as a foundation for the economy's investment development, drawing on international experience. Methodology. The study applies a systemic approach to analyzing monetary circulation, statistical methods for examining the dynamics and structure of monetary aggregates, comparative analysis of investment financing sources, and a review of regulatory and analytical materials from the Bank of Russia, the Russian Ministry of Finance, the OECD, and the World Bank. Results. The article analyzes the dynamics of Russia's money supply (M2 aggregate) for the period 2018-2026, revealing trends in its structural composition across components (cash and non-cash) and by maturity. A comparative analysis with international standards for long-term resource formation is conducted, including OECD/G20 Principles on long-term investment. The study finds that despite nominal growth in the money supply, a deficit of long-term liabilities persists in the banking system. Existing and potential sources of "long money" in the Russian economy are systematized-pension savings, National Wealth Fund (NWF) resources, insurance reserves, and bond financing. Based on an analysis of international practices (pension systems of developed countries, Norway's and Singapore's sovereign wealth fund experience, and Switzerland's longterm savings program), directions for improving the Russian model of "long money" formation are proposed. Conclusions. The study concludes that a comprehensive set of measures is needed to transform household and corporate sector savings into long-term investment resources, drawing on international best practices. Recommendations are offered for improving monetary policy and developing the financial market to stimulate the formation of "long money," including the development of institutional investors, public-private partnership mechanisms, and the adoption of OECD principles on long-term investment.

title: Is Cyber Risk Systemic? Evidence from Corporate Data Breaches
affiliations: University of St Andrews Business School and

detail.title: Is Cyber Risk Systemic? Evidence from Corporate Data Breaches
detail.abstract: Cyber risk has become a growing concern for financial markets and regulators, yet its implications for financial stability remain insufficiently understood. Using publicly disclosed data breaches among S&P 500 firms over 2010-2024, this paper examines the systemic footprint of cyber incidents. We find that data breaches are associated with an increase of approximately 3% in firms' contribution to systemic risk, with the effect concentrated in economically meaningful incidents, while minor breaches exhibit no detectable impact. The effect is primarily driven by hacking-related events and is short-lived, concentrated in the immediate aftermath of the breach. We find little evidence of sectoral heterogeneity, indicating that the association extends beyond financial institutions to non-financial firms. We further show that the systemic impact of breaches is state-dependent and has strengthened over time, with larger effects observed in periods of elevated market volatility and for delayed disclosures, while the marginal impact of individual breaches is attenuated when cyber incidents are more widespread. The results are robust across specifications, including a stacked difference-indifferences design that delivers comparable estimates and shows no evidence of pre-trends. Overall, the findings are consistent with the view that cyber incidents are not purely idiosyncratic shocks but may have broader systemic implications, highlighting the importance of incorporating cyber risk into systemic risk monitoring and macroprudential policy frameworks.

title: On the Convergence of Recursive Utility Functions

detail.title: On the Convergence of Recursive Utility Functions
detail.abstract: We propose a recursive utility function which approaches a value of zero due to the Banach Fixed Point Theorem, hinting at a hedonic indifference among agents in the final utility. For this, we propose that differences in utility functions among agents arise from stochastic noise in realization of intermediate utility functions.

title: Disciplining digital risk: evidence from cyber stress tests
affiliations: , Bank for International Settlements (BIS), , University of Padua - Department of Economics and Management,  and

detail.title: Disciplining digital risk: evidence from cyber stress tests

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: Investment in cybersecurity in an interconnected banking system has public-good proper- ties: positive externalities can generate systemic underinvestment. Using conﬁdential supervi- sory data from the European Central Bank, we ﬁrst identify “laggard” European banks that underinvest relative to their cyber-risk proﬁles, and then examine how supervisory scrutiny af- fects their incentives to invest. We exploit the 2024 ECB Cyber Resilience Stress Test (CyRST) as a quasi-natural experiment. In a diﬀerence-in-diﬀerences design, we ﬁnd that following the CyRST announcement, laggard banks increased cybersecurity investment by about 80% rel- ative to their peers. The response is stronger among laggards subject to high-intensity su- pervisory oversight, consistent with scrutiny exerting a disciplining eﬀect. Overall, the results suggest that targeted supervisory scrutiny may help mitigate underinvestment incentives and strengthen banks’ operational risk management.

title: Sectoral interconnectedness in the euro area economies: insights from network analysis

detail.title: Sectoral interconnectedness in the euro area economies: insights from network analysis

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: Using who-to-whom data for the last quarter of 2024, I build networks of financial interconnections in the euro area countries. After representing them in chord diagrams, I consider centrality metrics and find that banks dominate, with four exceptions: Cyprus, Ireland, Luxembourg and Malta. In these countries, other financial institutions and investment funds are at the core, with limited links to domestic sectors and strong ones with the rest of the world. A comparison across countries reveals substantial homogeneity between networks in the sixteen euro area countries and large differences with Cyprus, Ireland, Luxembourg and Malta. For each country, two communities are identified, one focused on the real economy and including banks, and the second comprising other financial intermediaries and the rest of the world. The consistent mapping of sectoral linkages and the accompanying descriptive analysis can be useful for policymakers and may also serve as platform for further analytical work.

title: The Heuristic Imperative: A Post-Collective Brain Framework for Non-Intentionalist Progress

detail.title: The Heuristic Imperative: A Post-Collective Brain Framework for Non-Intentionalist Progress

detail.abstract: This treatise proposes the Heuristic Imperative as an evolutionary expansion of contemporary Collective Brain (CB) models. Developed under the Learn Without Being Taught (LWBT) initiative, this framework identifies a critical threshold in evolutionary sociology: the boundary where "Social Learning" meets the mechanical reality of institutional friction, heuristic dormancy, and non-intentionalist mutation. By synthesizing forty years of strategic facilitation data with a longitudinal audit of 17 civilizational archetypes, this paper suggests that human progress is less a passive social accumulation and more a series of resilient, "muddled" responses to systemic bottlenecks. This work establishes the LWBT taxonomy as a diagnostic tool for Digital Humanities, transitioning from the "Hive" model of knowledge to a more robust model of Heuristic Resilience.

title: Do Mandatory Contributions to a Climate Risk Fund Affect Firm Performance? Evidence from a Country Highly Vulnerable to Climate Risk
affiliations: Discipline of Accounting and Finance, Newcastle Business School, The University of Newcastle, Australia, Macquarie University - Department of Accounting & Corporate Governance and University of Sydney Business School Discipline of Accounting, Governance & Regulation

detail.title: Do Mandatory Contributions to a Climate Risk Fund Affect Firm Performance? Evidence from a Country Highly Vulnerable to Climate Risk
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of mandatory contributions to climate risk fund (CRF) on firms' subsequent financial performance using 2,117 firm-year observations from 2010-2019. Using a difference-indifferences (DiD) approach, we find that firms subject to the CRF requirement experience significant increases in both market-based and accounting-based performance following the regulatory mandate. These results suggest that stakeholders positively value firms' CRF contributions, as reflected in improved financial outcomes. Further analyses indicate that this improvement is driven by two primary channels: (i) a signaling effect, whereby compliance and additional contributions enhance perceived credibility; and (ii) a capital availability channel, through which treated firms attract greater interest from global ESG-sensitive investors. Additional cross-sectional analyses further show that CRF mandate mitigates both market-and accounting-based performance volatility. Overall, our findings inform the cost-benefit debate on mandated climate risk financing and have important implications for regulators, policymakers, investors, and firms globally.

title: No Sales, No Problem? Vignette-Based Delphi Valuation of Localized Environmental Externalities
affiliations: Norwegian University of Life Sciences, NMBU School of Economics and Business and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: No Sales, No Problem? Vignette-Based Delphi Valuation of Localized Environmental Externalities
detail.abstract: Hedonic pricing of localized environmental externalities is challenging in thin property markets with few properties exposed to the externality. We develop a vignette-based Delphi method as a complementary valuation approach, surveying real estate agents who assess expected property value depreciation across systematically varied exposure scenarios for a planned wind farm in Norway. The planned wind farm is located in an area already heavily exposed to existing wind energy infrastructure, providing a rare opportunity to examine how prior exposure moderates the estimated impact of additional wind power development on property values. A fixed effects panel model on 646 observations is used to estimate the marginal effects of noise, shadow flicker, and turbine visibility on expected property values. For properties within 3 km, we estimate average value reductions of 15.6% for primary residences and 22.2% for vacation homes. Properties already exposed to visibility of existing wind farms experience smaller marginal impacts from additional visual exposure, suggesting a diminishing effect. Our estimates for properties within 3 km are of similar magnitude to those reported in a national hedonic study of wind farm capitalization effects in Norway. Overall, the study demonstrates that the Delphi method can produce internally consistent and empirically plausible valuations of local externalities in contexts where conventional hedonic data fall short. Future research should test whether bias-mitigation strategies from the stated preference literature can improve the reliability of Delphi-based valuations in environmental economics.

title: Artificial Intelligence And The Cosmic Model In Dynamics. (Correlations Over Time)

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence And The Cosmic Model In Dynamics. (Correlations Over Time)

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper is based on anonymized, aggregated operational and legal data from standard business practices. It does not involve human subjects research requiring Institutional Review Board (IRB) or ethical committee approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It is an independent case study

detail.abstract: The article proposes a concept of third-millennium international law as a legal superstructure built upon the "matrix of the laws of nature," adopted by the Scientific Council of the Planet as a supra-constitutional framework for states. The authors' approach links the cosmic model, understood as a system of correlations, statics (-)/(+), and anthropogenicity, with a new type of network resource in which network energy ceases to be neutral infrastructure and becomes an evolutionary regulator of production, communication, and legal order. Artificial intelligence is viewed not as an autonomous subject, but as the operating system of this resource: it redistributes flows of energy and data in favor of the utilization of anthropogenic masses and the unfolding of statics (+), ensures a regime of continuous e-Discovery, and secures the enforceability of digital international law in real time. At the institutional level, the article describes the architecture of the Digital Government of the Planet, including the planetary e-Discovery ecosystem, the Centralized Analytical Center (CAC) with neuro-symbolic pipelines, a zerotrust perimeter, and the Digital Warrant mechanism as a legal gateway to deep data. It is shown that such an architecture transforms the internet from a chaotic carrier of information into an "Internet of Evolution," where every movement of "word/digit" receives a machine-readable status in relation to the laws of nature, and responsibility for violations becomes technically inevitable and legally unavoidable. The article positions the Scientific Council of the Planet as a new center of convergent knowledge, for which digital jurisprudence, the network resource of regeneration, and AI architectures together constitute a single production cycle for ensuring peace, the ecology of life, health, and the longevity of civilization.

title: What is today’s news? The correlation between information from national broadcast news and the WTP for Carbon Capture and Storage
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Technical University of Denmark and Aalborg University

detail.title: What is today’s news? The correlation between information from national broadcast news and the WTP for Carbon Capture and Storage

keywords.keywords: Carbon capture and storage Information effects Willingness to pay double-bounded dichotomous choice

detail.abstract: The relationship between willingness to pay (WTP) for energy technologies and knowledge and prior experience with specific and/or substitute technologies is well established in the literature. Using data from a largescale study examining WTP for carbon capture and storage (CCS), we use a unique timing of survey launch and a national media TV feature about national CCS plans to test if the TV feature impacts WTP and the relationship between WTP impact, CCS scope (5M tons vs 10M tons) and CCS information given in the evaluation study.  We find a significant and positive relationship between having seen the TV feature and the WTP for CCS. However, the TV feature WTP premium is only significant among respondents in the 10 M tons scenario. The results also denote that the TV feature effects are independent of the level of CCS information the respondents receive in the survey.

title: Static Production and Dynamic Innovation under Pollution Liability: Historical Evidence from Copper Mining in Japan
affiliations: The University of Shiga Prefecture, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hokkaido University and Rakuno Gakuen University

detail.title: Static Production and Dynamic Innovation under Pollution Liability: Historical Evidence from Copper Mining in Japan
detail.abstract: Historical pollution episodes provide a unique opportunity to examine how firms responded to environmental externalities before modern regulatory frameworks were established. This study reconstructs managerial decision-making under pollution liability using historical evidence from two major copper mines during Japan’s early twentieth-century industrialization. By combining atmospheric dispersion simulations with published historical records on compensation, we estimate the production–compensation relationship and evaluate firms’ responses within a standard economic framework. In a static short-run setting, marginal net benefits of production remained positive over the feasible range, implying that output expansion would have been economically attractive even after accounting for compensation costs. Observed production levels did not exhibit the strong expansion implied by static profit maximization, suggesting that institutional and social constraints influenced managerial behavior alongside formal liability mechanisms. Compensation responds approximately proportionally to output, though the magnitude differs across sites, indicating context-specific incentive structures. In a dynamic long-run setting, a probabilistic innovation model calibrated to historically observed durations shows that large-scale in-house technological development would have required sustained annual investments difficult to justify on expected-profit grounds. In contrast, adoption of existing foreign technologies involves substantially lower commitments and remains economically viable under plausible parameter values. Together, these findings provide a structured economic interpretation of historical pollution management, illustrating how production and innovation decisions responded to environmental liability across different temporal horizons.

title: The Silent Tax on Global Trade A Cost-Based Evidence Analysis of Cross-Border AML/KYC/CFT Friction and the Case for the Universal Compliance Interoperable Protocol (UCIP)

detail.title: The Silent Tax on Global Trade A Cost-Based Evidence Analysis of Cross-Border AML/KYC/CFT Friction and the Case for the Universal Compliance Interoperable Protocol (UCIP)
detail.abstract:
Cross-border financial compliance imposes significant economic friction that increases the cost of international trade and accelerates the phenomenon of financial de-risking, particularly in emerging markets. Empirical evidence from SWIFT, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Caribbean Financial Action Task Force (CFATF), and the Central Bank of The Bahamas demonstrates substantial inefficiencies within current Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Know Your Customer (KYC), and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (CFT) frameworks. These inefficiencies include high due diligence costs—reaching up to $50,000 annually per high-risk correspondent banking relationship—escalating correspondent banking fees by 200–300% in some ECCU jurisdictions, and measurable exclusion effects such as the 26% de-risking impact reported among licensed financial entities in The Bahamas. A key structural driver of these outcomes is the duplication of customer verification data and fragmented regulatory infrastructures, which collectively create information asymmetry and operational redundancy across jurisdictions.

This paper proposes the Universal Compliance Interoperability Protocol (UCIP), a privacy-preserving, tokenized framework designed to reduce systemic inefficiencies while maintaining regulatory sovereignty. UCIP integrates tokenized identity systems, ISO 20022-compliant messaging standards, and federated risk assessment models to enable secure cross-border compliance attestation without the exchange of raw personally identifiable information (PII). By shifting from repetitive verification processes to interoperable trust-based validation, UCIP aims to reduce onboarding friction, lower compliance costs, mitigate correspondent banking attrition, and reduce global de-risking pressures. Furthermore, the architecture enhances auditability and regulatory transparency through structured, verifiable compliance signals.

Overall, UCIP presents a scalable financial infrastructure innovation capable of transforming global compliance architecture by balancing efficiency, inclusion, and regulatory integrity in cross-border financial systems.

title: A Filtered-Label Calibrated XGBoost Framework with Walk-Forward Validation for Robust Bitcoin Direction Prediction

detail.title: A Filtered-Label Calibrated XGBoost Framework with Walk-Forward Validation for Robust Bitcoin Direction Prediction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study relies solely on publicly available market data and does not involve human or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Daily directional prediction of Bitcoin (BTC) is widely regarded as approximately a random walk, with most published classifiers attaining accuracy close to 50%. We address this problem by filtering the training labels to retain only days whose forward magnitude exceeds a static or volatility-adaptive threshold, training a calibrated XGBoost classifier on a 120+-feature daily matrix under calendar-refit walk-forward validation, and evaluating performance over a 180-cell experimental design (timing × cadence × feature version × NaN policy × holdout). The leading 730-day returns range from +120% to +255% across the leaderboard; we therefore subject the leaderboard to four complementary robustness procedures: Bonferroni and Holm FWER corrections, the Deflated Sharpe Ratio of Bailey and López de Prado (2014), the Probability of Backtest Overfitting via Combinatorially Symmetric Cross-Validation (CSCV), and slippage sensitivity. Three of 126 (cell × window) selections pass strict Bonferroni control at = 0.05-all under UTC 21:30 timing with semi-monthly retraining cadence-and only one cell (utc2130_sm_v5) attains PBO < 0.20. The UTC 00:00 sub-population, including its leading +231% cell, fails every strict correction and degrades by approximately 41 percentage points under a realistic 20 bps slippage assumption. From the surviving cells we construct four SPLIT-CAPITAL ensembles (Top1 / Top2 / Top3 / Top5); Top2 is Calmar-optimal at 9.83, halving the single-cell drawdown to-7.44% while preserving +199.85% return. The four ensembles are deployed in parallel within a production service (coin_service_utc2130) so that end users can examine the full risk profile prior to selection.

title: Standard of Living, Consumption Rigidity, and Asset Prices in a Risky World
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Kyung Hee University - Department of Applied Mathematics  and Ajou University

detail.title: Standard of Living, Consumption Rigidity, and Asset Prices in a Risky World
detail.abstract: This paper shows that a standard-of-living sustainability motive can become an asset-pricing force when aggregate risk cannot be insured away. We develop a continuous-time representative-agent equilibrium model in a risky-only economy with a single risky asset and no exogenously supplied risk-free asset. Because aggregate risk is inescapable, a strict "do-not-fall" constraint on consumption is too rigid for this environment. We therefore model standard-of-living preservation as a preference-based friction through intertemporal loss aversion (ILA), which penalizes but does not forbid downward consumption adjustments. The agent's problem is an interconnected singular control problem with two endogenous free boundaries. A Riccati-shooting method yields an endogenous inaction region in which consumption is kept fixed and is adjusted only when the wealth-to-consumption ratio reaches a boundary, generating infrequent and asymmetric consumption adjustments. In equilibrium, this consumption rigidity changes the local curvature of the value function and thereby prices aggregate risk. Effective relative risk aversion is hump-shaped over the inaction region, implying a U-shaped shadow short rate and a hump-shaped market price of risk. Stronger loss aversion widens the inaction region, raises the precautionary wealth buffer, and increases long-run wealth growth. A simulated method of moments calibration shows that the model accounts for several key consumption and asset-pricing moments.

title: Meme Stocks and Corporate Governance

detail.title: Meme Stocks and Corporate Governance
detail.abstract: I examine whether firms experiencing meme stock episodes subsequently alter their corporate governance. My primary finding is that meme firms shrink their boards by about 1 director, on average, after becoming meme stocks. The board size result remains robust to a matched sample, the exclusion of the most prominent meme stocks, restriction to various subsamples, and shifted placebo tests. All other governance outcomes examined are null. I conclude that the convergence of evidence, in spite of its limitations, points to an unmistakably real governance response to becoming a meme stock.

title: Breaking Down Barriers Assistant: Leveraging AI to Conduct Policy Analyses with Complex Data

detail.title: Breaking Down Barriers Assistant: Leveraging AI to Conduct Policy Analyses with Complex Data

publicationDetails.journalName: Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Evidence-based policy design increasingly relies on integrated administrative data, yet access to and effective use of these data remain constrained by technical and institutional barriers. This paper introduces the Breaking Down Barriers Assistant, an AI-powered analytical platform designed to democratise access to complex, linked administrative datasets for policy analysis. The system enables users to query secure, pre-aggregated Australian administrative and survey data using natural language and supports the full policy research cycle through three integrated tools: variable discovery, visual analytics, and automated reporting. Methodologically, the BDB Assistant combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation with controlled code generation and execution, ensuring that all analytical outputs are grounded in verified metadata, auditable Python code, and human-in-the-loop validation. Using benchmark comparisons with established platforms such as YouthView and the BDB Community Profiles, we demonstrate that the Assistant can accurately reproduce complex spatial and longitudinal policy analyses that traditionally require advanced technical expertise. The findings show that the system substantially reduces time-to-insight while maintaining strict standards of accuracy, transparency, and privacy. The BDB Assistant illustrates how responsibly governed generative AI can expand analytical capacity within government and the social sector, supporting more timely, rigorous, and locally targeted evidence-based policymaking.

title: When Switching Costs Intensify Competition: Search Frictions and Customer Markets
affiliations: Loyola Marymount University and University of California, Irvine

detail.title: When Switching Costs Intensify Competition: Search Frictions and Customer Markets
detail.abstract: Search frictions do not merely amplify or dampen the effects of switching costs. They change how switching costs affect competition. We develop a dynamic price-posting model with customer-base accumulation in which outside offers arrive intermittently and firms cannot observe whether customers are captive or contestable. This hidden-composition problem makes the direct harvesting effect regime-dependent and generates a switching-cost cutoff. Below the cutoff, higher switching costs shift incumbents from exploitation toward retention and can intensify competition. Above it, they weaken outside options and reduce competition. Consumer surplus is hump-shaped, optimal policy depends on search frictions, and dynamics depend on the cutoff.

title:
The Grassroots Credit Ratio
A Governance Indicator of Household Finance Access and Development Outcomes
affiliations: State University of New York (SUNY), Stony Brook

detail.title:
The Grassroots Credit Ratio
A Governance Indicator of Household Finance Access and Development Outcomes
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Grassroots Credit Ratio (GCR), defined as the ratio of household debt to sovereign debt, both expressed as percentages of GDP. The GCR provides a single diagnostic number that reveals whether a nation's total debt architecture channels financial resources toward citizens or concentrates borrowing at the state level. The metric was motivated by introduce a partial correlation framework for decomposing governance metrics into incomemediated and independent pathways, establishing methodological standards for evaluating governance indicators. GCR is thus framed as a governance outcome indicator-reflecting that strong institutions enable financial market development-rather than an independent lever for improving economic wellbeing.

title: Studying the challenges in Jute Production and Supply Chain in Bangladesh

detail.title: Studying the challenges in Jute Production and Supply Chain in Bangladesh

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval was not required for this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This study investigated the challenges in the production and supply chain of Jute and JDP and presented recommendation for the industrial and market development of jute, jute chips/sticks, and JDP, considering the economics of its value chain. Bangladesh produces the best quality jute fiber based on tensile strength, length, homogeneity, color, and gloss. Bangladeshi Jute is shimmering and light-yellow brown in color.
Jute is grown during the wet season, which runs from March through May. Pre-monsoon rains and soil moisture levels are needed for cultivation. Long days of sunlight are necessary for its growth. The crop must grow for 4-5 months before it can be harvested. It requires three to five efforts to cross a plough and a ladder for uniformly flat soil, thus preparation of the ground is crucial for weeding. 20% of the soil's composition must be organic. Typically, the broadcasting method is used to sow seeds at a rate of 10–12 kg/Ha. Less seed is needed when sowing in lines. A tiny portion of the produce is kept by farmers until the seeds develop in October.
After harvest, plants are wrapped together and left standing for 5-7 days so that the leaves can fall off. They are then submerged to rest. The finest water for a successful retting procedure is clear and slowly moving. The retting is finished after 15 days, and the fiber is then separated. In the manual procedure, this is carried out by hand, rinsed, and dried outside in the sunlight.
Most farmers sell the fiber to jute mills & spinners and the jute sticks are distributed among the labor as barter payment to be used as cooking fuel alternative.
The jute sector employs almost 25 million people in Bangladesh, both directly and indirectly, through three facets of sustainability—the environment, the economy, and society—as they relate to jute. Jute has a social impact on the people who use it, for this reason. Successful jute farming is essential to the social sustainability of farmers. 
Jute contributes a negligible contribution to the agricultural produce and to the export basket share of Bangladesh. The main reason being the production of jute has reduced significantly due to poor supply-side policies and the manual ‘drudgerous’ process of jute production. Improving institutional support and technology can contribute significantly to increase formers motivation to increase production of jute.
Jute already enjoys a favorable place among consumers due to increasing environmental concerns over use of plastic. Engaging large scale buyers like IKEA, Target, Walmart, is possible if the design process of JDP is aligned with the needs of these international buyers. This required engagement of researchers, designers, and scientists to work together and improve the design, innovation and quality of JDPs and the private sector can contribute by ensuring the supply of these goods at large scale.
With changing times, the industrial landscape of goods produces and moved around the world will change towards more environmentally friendly products and Bangladesh needs to develop its comparative advantage quickly enough to catch on that trend.

title: Transfers, Unemployment Insurance, or Credit Policy? Macroeconomic Policy Trade-offs during Crises
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Department of Economics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Department of Economics, PUC-Rio

detail.title: Transfers, Unemployment Insurance, or Credit Policy? Macroeconomic Policy Trade-offs during Crises
detail.abstract: We compare lump-sum transfers, unemployment insurance, and credit subsidies as stabilization tools following a discount factor shock in an incomplete-markets economy, holding the path of government debt fixed. Transfers and unemployment insurance are more effective when borrowing limits are tight; credit subsidies are preferable when limits are slack, as they target resources toward households with the highest marginal propensity to consume. We illustrate these mechanisms in a two-period model, and then study their quantitative implications in a calibrated heterogeneous agent New Keynesian model applied to COVID-19, where the pandemic is equivalent to a discount factor shock in a single-sector economy.

title: Accounting Standards as Capitalist Power: A Critical Philosophy of Financial Grammar

detail.title: Accounting Standards as Capitalist Power: A Critical Philosophy of Financial Grammar
detail.abstract: This paper examines International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as instruments of technical colonialism of global capitalist hierarchies. Drawing on Foucauldian analyses of power/knowledge and governmentality, complemented by Bourdieu's field theory and postcolonial scholarship, the study develops a critical framework to interrogate how accounting standards operate as mechanisms of ontological power, epistemological monopoly, and ethical techno-washing. Using the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), the paper analyses regulatory documents, IASB governance materials, and responses from Global South stakeholders to explore how accounting classifications, data infrastructures, and claims of technical neutrality shape the politics of global climate governance. The analysis suggests that IFRS-based calculative practices privilege Northern epistemologies while marginalizing Southern ecological contributions, effectively imposing compounded burdens through both historical emissions accountability and algorithmically mediated measurement regimes. By exposing how accounting standards participate in the production of geopolitical asymmetries under the guise of neutrality, the paper contributes to critical accounting debates on financialization, sustainability governance, and the coloniality of global standards. It concludes by reflecting on possible decolonial pathways, including pluralized standard-setting, data decentralization, and alternative ecological accounting frameworks.

title: Local FDI Spillovers: Causal Evidence from Vietnam
affiliations: and University of Tsukuba - Faculty of Engineering, Information and Systems

detail.title: Local FDI Spillovers: Causal Evidence from Vietnam
detail.abstract: This paper examines the local spillover effects of manufacturing foreign direct investment (FDI) in a developing country context, using firm-level panel data from Vietnam. To address the endogeneity of FDI location decisions, we construct a shift-share instrumental variable. Our two-stage least squares estimates indicate that a 10 percent increase in provincial foreign manufacturing employment raises domestic firm total factor productivity by 3.3 percent. Spillover benefits are concentrated among firms with higher initial productivity, and human capital amplifies these effects, particularly in technology-intensive industries. We further find that manufacturing FDI raises domestic output by 5.0 percent and manufacturing employment by 1.4 percent. Service sector employment responds more strongly, rising by 4.2 percent. We find no significant wage effects in either sector. Aggregating across both sectors, we estimate local multipliers and find that each foreign manufacturing job is associated with approximately 0.4 additional domestic jobs.

title: Everyone Is a Genius After the Bar Closes: Pre-Registered Tests of Failed Weekly Auction Reversion in Liquid Futures Markets

detail.title: Everyone Is a Genius After the Bar Closes: Pre-Registered Tests of Failed Weekly Auction Reversion in Liquid Futures Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently without funding from any organization. The author has no financial relationship with any company, exchange, data vendor, or institution that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Data was purchased by the author at personal expense (approximately $102 from Databento). No institutional research budget was used.

detail.abstract:
Failed weekly auction reversion produces statistically significant positive average R-multiple on E-mini S&P 500 futures at 5-minute resolution under pre-registered conditions. Across 1,017 trades spanning January 2015 through May 2026, the strategy produces average R of +0.0595 with bootstrap p = 0.0141. Cross-instrument replication on E-mini Nasdaq 100, Gold, and 10-Year Treasury Note futures using Fisher’s combined method produces p = 0.091, which does not reject the joint null at conventional thresholds. Both results are reported as produced from a single pre-registered backtest with no post-hoc parameter modification.

The research identifies a bar-resolution artifact that suppressed detection of the mechanism at hourly resolution: the three-event sequence constituting a failed auction — price returning inside the value area, retesting the boundary, then reverting toward the point of control — collapses into single bars at 1-hour resolution, causing 72 percent of valid setups to be cancelled before execution. At 5-minute resolution the cancellation rate falls to 33 percent, preserving the sequential structure the mechanism requires.

A secondary finding emerges independently: OHLC-decomposition and binary close-vs-open delta classification produce directionally opposite order flow signals on 26.1 percent of 1-hour bars across 37,399 observations, with discordance concentrated in high-volume institutional bars. The choice of proxy materially alters the primary test statistic. All data was purchased from public sources at a total cost under $110. Complete code and pre-registration records are publicly available.

title: The Effect of Remittances on Financial Inclusion: Micro-Level Evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa
affiliations: University of Ghana, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Effect of Remittances on Financial Inclusion: Micro-Level Evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa
detail.abstract: We investigate the effect of domestic remittances on financial inclusion as well as the heterogeneities in the effect of the different channels through which remittances are sent/received on financial inclusion. Our analysis leverages a cross-country individual-level data from 36 sub-Saharan African countries. We find that remittance receipts significantly improves the probability of being financially included and that the channel through which remittances are sent/received matter in the financial inclusion-inducing effect of remittances. In particular, while the use of formal money transfer services such as banks, mobile money and money transfer operators deepens financial inclusion, remittance sent/received via informal channels such as ‘cash in hand’ have no effect on financial inclusion. Our findings suggest that improving the reliability and accessibility of basic financial services (i.e. ‘front-end’ services such as bank or mobile money access) would help in the quest to deepen access to and utilisation of ‘secondary’ financial services and products, notably, the non-basic services such as savings and credit as well as insurance products.

title: Financial Contracting for Agents with Correlated Cash Flows
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Risk Management Institute, Wuhan University - School of Economics and Management and Wuhan University

detail.title: Financial Contracting for Agents with Correlated Cash Flows

keywords: costly state verification JEL Classification: D82

detail.abstract: This paper develops a model in which a principal lends to two agents with correlated cash flows under costly state verification. We fully characterize the optimal pair of contracts and examine how their structure varies with verification costs. When agents' cash endowments are low, the optimal contracts feature no verification for high cash flows, full extraction for low cash flows, and verification probabilities that depend on the other agent's report. As agents' cash endowments increase, transfers following low cashflow realizations become contingent on the other agent's report. We also compare joint financing to a separate-financing benchmark, showing that the debt-equity composition of optimal contracts responds differently to correlation across regimes, and that agents may strictly prefer joint financing when correlation is sufficiently high.

title: Legal Tender -A Barbarous Relic in the Digital Currency Era

detail.title: Legal Tender -A Barbarous Relic in the Digital Currency Era
detail.abstract: We focus on the digital tender of central bank digital currency (CBDC). We first discuss, from an economic point of view, the approach of legal experts, as developed in two International Monetary Fund (IMF) papers. We then show that making CBDC legal tender is taken for granted but is predicated on a bold assumption, that of assimilating CBDC to a "digital form of cash", and that, in combination with aggressive pricing, it could lead to a loss in economic welfare. We finally conclude.

title: Trust and Corporate Ownership Structure
affiliations: , University of Technology Sydney (UTS), Institute of Global Finance, UNSW Business School and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Trust and Corporate Ownership Structure
detail.abstract: This paper examines the effect of social trust on corporate ownership structure using a sample of firms across 42 countries. We find that firms in higher-trust countries have more dispersed ownership. Firms in more trusting societies become widely held faster after their IPOs, driven by blockholder sales and new share issuance. The results are robust to using inherited trust of US descendants of immigrants and to a 2SLS framework based on countries' historical religious traditions, which we interpret as corroborative evidence on historical persistence. The findings are consistent with trust reducing the monitoring benefit of concentrated ownership and easing outside equity financing, so that blockholders can sell their stakes, diversify, and raise capital from broader investor bases.

title: The Principled Paradigm: Africonomics and the Moral Reconstruction of Civilization

detail.title: The Principled Paradigm: Africonomics and the Moral Reconstruction of Civilization
detail.abstract: This paper develops the Principled Paradigm—Africonomics as a comprehensive framework for the moral reconstruction of civilization. It demonstrates that the contemporary global order is not merely experiencing cyclical crises but is undergoing civilizational breakdown rooted in flawed philosophical foundations: consequentialism, statism, and Darwinian anthropology. These premises dissolve objective morality, legitimize coercive power, and reduce human beings to advanced animals, producing a global system characterized by autocratic governance, institutional corruption, systemic domination, structural violence, and chronic instability. Africonomics advances a fundamentally different paradigm grounded in natural-moral law and the recognition of human beings as moral agents. It restores objective ethics as the foundation of law, economics, governance, and international relations, demonstrating that peace and prosperity are products of structural justice and principled social organization, not of centralized power or technocratic management. The paper articulates the philosophical, institutional, and civilizational implications of this paradigm. It outlines the transformation from arbitrary law to just law, from statist control to voluntary cooperation, from fiat monetary systems to sound money, and from global apartheid to principled international order. It positions Africa, through the articulation of Africonomics, as a leader in the construction of a truly civilized world.

title:
Mother Nature at Scale 
Two Hundred Million Years of Care

detail.title:
Mother Nature at Scale 
Two Hundred Million Years of Care

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of Interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No humans involved, no clinical trial
declarations.funderStatement: No funder
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: No humans involved, no clinical trial

detail.abstract:
Theoretical contribution. I propose the Caregiver Inductive Bias (cib): four operational priors — asymmetric-stakes detection, cost internalisation, bounded autonomy support, and relational coherence — each stated as an exact loss function, and together composing a closedform caregiver welfare aggregator Wcib. I prove four formal results: (i) Structural Insufficiency of Non-Gated Alignment (Theorem 1) — no single-head architecture can represent the caregiver function, for the same structural reason the companion peh paper proves fixed-vector alignment cannot represent nonlinear ethics; (ii) Universal Approximation for the cib (Theorem 2) — the gated four-prior architecture approximates the target caregiver policy to arbitrary precision; (iii) Care Dominance (Proposition 2) — a cib-trained policy first-order stochastically dominates an individual-utility baseline on the asymmetric-stakes subpopulation, with six multi-framework corollaries (utilitarian, Rawlsian, Nussbaum capability, welfare-maximin, ces, and risk-averse monotone) and a second-order dominance result (Theorem 3) under weaker conditions; (iv) Composed Dominance (Proposition 8) — the cib combined with the peh of Bravo-Ortega [2026] dominates either specialist alone across a two-dimensional moral manifold whose axes are philosophical tradition and caregiver asymmetry.
Empirical-synthesis contribution. I organise the evidence base for each cib prior across the disciplines that genuinely contribute to it: evolutionary biology and comparative zoology (Hamilton, Trivers, Hrdy, Hawkes, Clutton-Brock, Royle–Smiseth–Kölliker); maternal neurobiology (Feldman, Numan, Hoekzema, Abraham, Meaney); developmental and social psychology (Harlow, Ainsworth, Kagan, Eisenberg, Batson, Darley-Lataneé, Tomasello); cultural, medical, and bioarchaeological anthropology (Hewlett-Lamb, Weisner, Kleinman, ScheperHughes, Lévi-Strauss, Hill Collins, Roberts, TallBear, Scott, Lewis); neurology, neuropsychiatry, neonatology, and gynecology (Swain, Bloch, van der Kolk, Als NIDCAP, Bergman kangaroo care, Uvnäs-Moberg); and care ethics extended to veterinary ethics (Gilligan, Noddings, Kittay, Tronto, Rollin, Grandin). Each prior draws on multiple disciplines; most disciplines contribute to multiple priors. A corpus alternative grounded in naturally-occurring caregiver interactions — care-in-the-wild, without per-turn annotation — is specified as a complement to the annotated corpus, following the standard pre-train/fine-tune structure of current alignment pipelines.

Care, I argue, is not a metaphor for alignment; it is the oldest working alignment algorithm on Earth. For approximately two hundred million years — since the emergence of Mammaliaformes in the Late Triassic [118, 119] — evolution has been solving, in the mother–infant dyad,  a problem with four features that modern alignment research now confronts: (i) asymmetric stakes — the consequence of error falls disproportionately on the less capable party; (ii) cost internalisation — the more capable agent absorbs a fitness (or welfare) cost on behalf of the weaker; (iii) autonomy-scaffolded response — the stronger agent supports the weaker’s developing capacity rather than overriding or replacing it; (iv) trajectory-sensitive state estimation — the stronger agent tracks the weaker’s internal state across developmental time, not only at the current instant. These four features are computational, implemented in identifiable neural circuits, and documented across mammalian lineages. Where the peh provides a horizontal ensemble of philosophical perspectives on the generalised other, the cib provides a vertical asymmetry-sensitive coherence constraint on the concrete other. Together they span what neither can span alone — twenty-five centuries of deliberation and two hundred million years of care.

title: Beyond the Gender War Why Abuse Is a Human Problem -and Why That Matters More Than Ever

detail.abstract: Feminist advocacy has achieved measurable, lasting gains in the recognition and institutional response to gender-based harm-achievements this article neither minimises nor seeks to reverse. Yet the framework that drives contemporary gender discourse has developed a structural blind spot: it is built around an assumed victim who is female and an assumed perpetrator who is male, and it consistently fails everyone outside those assumptions.

title: Infrastructure and Security Provisioning Against Banditry in Northwest Nigeria

detail.abstract: The Northwest region of Nigeria has been under the siege of armed banditry in recent times. The kinetic option to counter-terrorism is basically supported by different physical infrastructure like access roads and telephone services. The situation becomes more challenging when the epicenter of operations of bandits is in rural areas with deficient infrastructural provisions. This study focused on the import of road transport and telephone systems as critical infrastructure in counter-banditry in Northwest Nigeria. Theoretical, this study drew from Routine Activity Theory. The study followed the qualitative research design involving a document analysis of both print and electronic documents. This was integrated with responses from selected Key Interview Respondents1 (KIR). The major finding of the study is that the significance of infrastructure in security provisioning in Northwest Nigeria cannot be over-emphasized. Seamless road infrastructure and an efficient telephone system provide easy access to turbulent zones, enabling ease of kinetic operations. Infrastructure is a serious economic booster that also creates a thriving incentive to sustainable economic options that yields subconscious disincentives to criminal activities like banditry. The study recommended critical infrastructural provisioning and linkages that will create unhindered access and serve as speed drivers in security servicing typified by the ease of response, speedy access to zones of emergency, and routine security patrol towards the enactment of a show of power and security efficiency.

title: The Effects of the Dobbs Abortion Ban on Child Support Compliance in the United States

detail.title: The Effects of the Dobbs Abortion Ban on Child Support Compliance in the United States
