detail.abstract: This paper presents the Cyber-Financial Risk Scoring and Anomaly Detection Framework-an integrated machine learning system combining unsupervised anomaly detection and supervised classification to proactively identify fraud and prevent improper payments in large-scale federal disbursement programs. The framework synthesizes audit-based financial control intelligence, predictive risk scoring, machine learning-driven anomaly detection, and cybersecurity risk analysis into a unified, modular, and scalable system. Validated against 508,213 financial transactions totaling over $101.4 billion in transaction value using the PaySim synthetic financial dataset, the framework achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.9994, Average Precision of 0.9980, and 100% precision on flagged transactions, successfully identifying $3.009 billion in fraudulent exposure.

title: The Financialization of Water Scarcity: Exchange Rate Dynamics and Virtual Water Flows in Wheat Trade
affiliations: and Mohammed V University of Rabat

detail.title: The Financialization of Water Scarcity: Exchange Rate Dynamics and Virtual Water Flows in Wheat Trade
detail.abstract: Water-stressed regions remain net exporters of virtual water, water volume embedded in traded goods to areas with abundant water resources, despite accelerating climate change impacts. We investigate whether exchange rate dynamics and systemic real exchange rate misalignments influence persistent imbalances in virtual water trade. We employ rigorous panel regressions with fixed or random effects on major wheat-exporting and importing countries, alongside relevant control variables. Our findings indicate that currency depreciations and persistent undervaluation stimulate exports and reduce imports of virtual water, thereby intensifying water outflows. Conversely, currency appreciations and sustained overvaluations increase virtual water imports and discourage exports, resulting in higher water inflows. These results suggest that exchange rate instability and misalignment indirectly contribute to transboundary water mining by channeling virtual water flows toward overvalued currencies. Policymakers should incorporate exchange rate management strategies into virtual water balances. Hedging instruments that mitigate depreciations, along with the avoidance of competitive devaluations, may prove essential for achieving water sustainability objectives.

title: The Last Mile of AI: Judgment Infrastructure, Defensible Audit Logs, and the End of Information Retrieval

detail.title: The Last Mile of AI: Judgment Infrastructure, Defensible Audit Logs, and the End of Information Retrieval

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Founder & CEO of askOdin Pte. Ltd. (UEN: 202531656N), a Singapore-incorporated company that develops the methodologies described in this paper, including the RUNE Protocol, the Clarity Framework™, the Judgment Graph™, and AI Judgment Infrastructure™. The author has operational and financial interest in the commercial deployment of these methodologies. Empirical metrics cited in this paper are drawn from live operational deployment of the RUNE Protocol within askOdin's infrastructure. No external funding was received for this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper presents conceptual framework analysis and aggregate operational metrics from proprietary infrastructure. No human subjects, patient data, or personally identifiable information were used in this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by askOdin Pte. Ltd. No external grants or sponsored funding contributed to this work.

detail.abstract: The proliferation of foundational Large Language Models has reduced the marginal cost of information retrieval and synthesis to zero. When every capital allocator operates from the same omniscient information baseline, information asymmetry ceases to generate alpha. This paper argues that the competitive frontier in capital allocation has fundamentally shifted: the premium is no longer on accessing data, but on the rigor with which logic derived from that data is stress-tested. We define this transition as the emergence of AI Judgment Infrastructure-a dedicated architecture for evaluating the structural soundness of investment theses, rather than merely retrieving and summarizing the information they contain. Drawing on a corpus of 60,000+ Clarity Scores benchmarked through the RUNE Protocol (patent-pending), we identify seven empirically derived archetypes of investment thesis failure-the Grammar of Failure-and introduce the Judgment Graph as a proprietary data structure mapping relationships between claims, evidence, and historical failure patterns. We further propose the Defensible Audit Log as the canonical output artifact of this infrastructure: an immutable, machine-verifiable proof of analytical rigor for institutional stakeholders. The Clarity Framework and The Rigor Protocol are presented as the applied methodology and organizational standard required to operationalize AI Judgment Infrastructure at scale. Our central thesis: judgment is the last unscalable asset, and the infrastructure we build today will determine who commands the next decade of capital deployment.

title: Capital Structure and Market Timing: International Evidence
affiliations: University of Waikato - Department of Economics and Finance and University of South Australia - UniSA Business School

detail.title: Capital Structure and Market Timing: International Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper provides new international evidence on how equity market valuations shape firms’ capital structure choices and how these effects persist across institutional environments and financial crises. Using a large panel of 7,816 publicly listed firms from 43 countries over 2005–2024, we document three central findings. First, while pooled estimates yield modest support for equity market timing, country‑level results show that valuation‑driven financing decisions have persistent effects on leverage in a substantial subset of countries, particularly those with well‑developed equity markets and stronger institutional quality. Second, firms with high market valuations systematically substitute toward equity issuance, but the persistence of these effects depends critically on market development and financing frictions, rather than on historical valuation measures alone. Third, exploiting major exogenous disruptions to debt markets—the Global Financial Crisis and the COVID‑19 shock—we provide causal evidence that valuation channels amplify leverage adjustments during periods of financial stress, especially for smaller and more constrained firms. Overall, the results reveal that equity market timing is neither uniformly transitory nor purely mechanical: its impact on capital structure is conditional on institutional structure, firm characteristics, and macro‑financial shocks. These findings underscore the central role of valuation dynamics in shaping leverage choices and reconcile previously mixed evidence by highlighting heterogeneity across countries and market conditions.

detail.abstract: Medicaid projected improper payments reached USD 37.4 billion in 2025. Despite a federal audit programme costing approximately USD 180 million annually, rigorous causal evidence on audit effectiveness remains limited. This study exploits the quasi-experimental variation created by the PERM three-year audit rotation cycle to estimate the causal effect of audit exposure on state-level improper payment rates. Using state-specific data from CMS PERM Supplemental Data Reports for all three available audit cycles, the adjusted pooled treatment effect is negative 3.84 percentage points, significant at the one per cent level with wild cluster bootstrap confirmation. Welfare analysis yields an estimated combined federal and state return on investment of 8.9 times the annual programme cost. Heterogeneous effects reveal that low-to-medium vulnerability states drive efficiency gains while the highest-quartile states show no improvement, supporting a shift from uniform to risk-stratified audit design. Isolation Forest anomaly detection using CMS drug utilization data is introduced as a proof-of-concept risk-scoring framework.

title: A BAYESIAN-KELLY PARETO FRONTIER FOR OPTIMAL TRANSACTION ACCEPTANCE UNDER UNCERTAINTY

detail.title: A BAYESIAN-KELLY PARETO FRONTIER FOR OPTIMAL TRANSACTION ACCEPTANCE UNDER UNCERTAINTY

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This research was conducted independently without any personal or financial relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a purely theoretical/methodological paper with no human participants, patients, or empirical data involving human subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
We synthesize the Kelly Criterion with Bayesian inference to characterize the optimal Go/No-Go decision boundary for transactions under uncertainty. Starting from the Kelly growth rate, we derive a hyperbolic Pareto frontier that converges to the simple expected-value threshold p · r > c. By modeling the probability of success p with a Beta(α, β) distribution — where α represents observed successes and β represents frictions — we show that any rational agent should accept a transaction if and only if the net profit ratio b exceeds the observed friction-to-success ratio β/α. 

This simple critical ratio provides an intuitive, mathematically grounded heuristic for decision-making in high-uncertainty environments such as sales, procurement, entrepreneurship, and supply chain transactions.

reference: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-09
title: The Chicago Fed Labor Market Indicators: Bridging the Gap with Alternative Labor Data
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago and Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago

detail.title: The Chicago Fed Labor Market Indicators: Bridging the Gap with Alternative Labor Data

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-09
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We present the Chicago Fed Labor Market Indicators (LMI): a twice-monthly release that includes the job-finding r ate, t he j ob-separation r ate, a nd a f orecast f or the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) unemployment rate. To overcome limitations in data availability, the LMI uses partial least squares to combine CPS-based finding and separation rates with higher-frequency alternative and traditional labor market data series-such as unemployment insurance claims, Google Trends searches, online job postings, and survey-based indicators. Our resulting flow-consistent unemployment rate (FCR) correlates strongly with the BLS unemployment rate, and can be used to characterize the current "low-hire, low-fire" n ature o f t he U .S. l abor m arket. We use a Bayesian linear regression centered on a no-change prior to translate changes in our FCR into a real-time forecast for the next BLS unemployment rate reading. In backtesting spanning 2018-2026, our unemployment rate forecast improves on both a random-walk benchmark and the Bloomberg consensus forecast, with the largest accuracy gains during the Covid-19 pandemic when the unemployment rate rose rapidly in a way that was well-captured by high-frequency labor market data.

reference: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2023-22
title: Learning Monetary Policy Strategies at the Effective Lower Bound with Sudden Surprises
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago - Economic Research, University of Warwick and Deutsche Bundesbank - Research Centre

detail.title: Learning Monetary Policy Strategies at the Effective Lower Bound with Sudden Surprises

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2023-22
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We examine how private sector agents might learn a new monetary strategy introduced while policy rates are at their effective lower bound (ELB) in an environment with large inflationary and deflationary shocks. We consider the adoption of a new asymmetric average inflation targeting rule aimed at countering the disinflationary bias imparted by the ELB. The most crucial time for learning runs from when rates would be near liftoff under the old strategy through early liftoff under the new rule. Recessionary shocks during this time could delay learning while large inflationary shocks could outright stop it, inhibiting the ability of the new strategy to address the costs associated with the ELB. Using the U.S. post-Covid experience as an example, we also find that the monetary policy shocks can have important feedback on the learning process.

keywords: A Computational Framework Integrating Behavioral States
and Competitive Front Allocations Alexandros Tsitsis (IES23176) Course: International Relations I Prof. Spyropoulos

Strategic Behavior Markov Models Colonel Blotto Monte Carlo Simulation Conflict Dynamics Computational IR Game Theory Resource Allocation Behavioral Modeling State Transition Models Strategic Competition

detail.abstract: This paper presents the 5-State Behavior Model, a computational framework for describing and comparing strategic behavior among international actors. The model defines five behavioral states-Assertion, Escalation, Confrontation, Retrenchment, and Normalizationand represents transitions among them through a first-order Markov process (Billingsley 1995). Each state is associated with a distinct allocation profile across competitive fronts, drawing on a simplified Colonel Blotto formulation (Roberson 2006). Monte Carlo simulations are used to generate probabilistic behavioral trajectories and steady-state distributions (Robert and Casella 2004), allowing the model to capture long-run tendencies implied by empirically estimated transition matrices. The framework is applied to five cases representing diverse strategic environments: the United States-China rivalry, Russia's post-2022 behavior, NATO as a collective actor, the India-Pakistan dyad, and a peaceful reference case (France-Denmark). The results demonstrate that the model identifies meaningful structural differences across competitive, institutional, and low-intensity settings. Competitive dyads exhibit recurrent cycles of Assertion and Escalation, Russia displays a long-run concentration in Confrontation and Retrenchment, NATO stabilizes around Assertion and Normalization, and the peaceful dyad converges almost entirely to Normalization. These findings highlight the model's capacity to represent both conflictual and cooperative environments without relying on causal assumptions or theoretical priors. The contribution of the study is methodological: it offers a neutral, reproducible, and comparable approach for mapping strategic behavior across international actors. The model provides a structured way to visualize behavioral tendencies, identify dominant transition cycles, and compare strategic environments, while avoiding claims about motives, preferences, or long-term intentions.

title: Liberty and State Effectiveness in Industrializing Britain: War, Politics, and Law
affiliations: Washington and Lee University - Department of Economics and Department of Economics

detail.title: Liberty and State Effectiveness in Industrializing Britain: War, Politics, and Law
detail.abstract: We examine the determinants of individual liberty and state effectiveness in industrializing Britain, analyzing both outcomes jointly within a unified empirical framework. Drawing on 67,453 reports of cases heard in the English law courts between 1765 and 1865, we use large language models (LLMs) to construct case-level measures of judicial orientation toward individual liberty and state effectiveness. We then relate these measures to war, partisan control of government, their interaction, and salient case characteristics. Both wartime conditions and Tory governments—and especially their conjunction—shift legal emphasis toward state effectiveness and away from individual liberty. Strikingly, neither common-law nor de jure judicial independence systematically promotes individual liberty, contrary to conventional views of the two pillars of English legal institutions. Appeals from India lead to an elevated emphasis on individual liberty, unlike cases involving the state as a litigant or other cases originating outside Britain. Methodologically, our analysis demonstrates the power of LLMs to extract nuanced institutional data from historical corpora.

title: Tracking the K‑Shaped Economy: Who’s Driving Spending?
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Federal Reserve Bank of New York

detail.title: Tracking the K‑Shaped Economy: Who’s Driving Spending?

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Aggregate real consumer spending has risen solidly since 2023. However, it is less clear how widely shared this improvement has been across all segments of society. This is important because systematic heterogeneity may mask the dependence of aggregate growth on a relatively small group of households and thus conceal macroeconomic risks. In this post, we use consumer spending data recently added to the Economic Heterogeneity Indicators (EHIs) and find that retail spending growth has been driven by high-income households—those earning more than $125,000 per year. In the popular press, the phenomenon of higher-income households growing at a faster rate than lower-income households has been referred to as the K-shaped economy. We find that consumption has exhibited a K-shaped economy since 2023, although not in the pre-COVID period or during the post-COVID recovery.

To view post:https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/05/tracking-the-k-shaped-economy-whos-driving-spending/

title: Golden Security: Analysing Future of Gold Investment in India

detail.abstract:
Gold has always occupied a special place in the economic and cultural life of India.

For centuries, it has been regarded not only as a symbol of wealth and social prestige

but also as a reliable form of financial security. In recent years, however, the role of

title: All-cause and External-cause Mortality Disparities Among Australians in Same-Sex Relationships Before and After Marriage Equality: A Nationwide Cohort Study, 2011-2023

detail.title: All-cause and External-cause Mortality Disparities Among Australians in Same-Sex Relationships Before and After Marriage Equality: A Nationwide Cohort Study, 2011-2023

publicationDetails.journalName: Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Objective: To examine secular trends in mortality by sexual orientation in Australia. Methods: Using Australian Census-linked-mortality records (2011-2023), Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate all-cause and external-cause mortality risk among adults in same-sex relationships (n=54,529) and different-sex relationships (n=7,923,328), separately by sex. Inverse probability weights balanced comparators on age, educational attainment, and household income. Results were stratified into periods before and after Australia's 2017 legalisation of same-sex marriage.

Results: Compared to those in different-sex relationships, females and males in same-sex relationships experienced elevated all-cause mortality risk [HR1.25 (95% CI 1.15;1.35) and HR1.24 (95%CI 1.16;1.31), respectively] and external-cause mortality risk [HR2.56 (95%CI 2.01;3.26) and HR1.96 (95%CI 1.64;2.71), respectively]. Inequalities in external-cause mortality risk declined following Marriage Equality among females (HR 3.40 → 2.04) and males (HR 2.01 → 1.93) in same-sex relationships, though remained significantly elevated in both periods.

Conclusions: Australians in same-sex relationships experience elevated mortality risk relative to those in different-sex relationships, with inequalities persisting after marriage equality. Routine collection of sexual identity in the Australian Census would support ongoing monitoring of these disparities.

title: Logarithmic Tax Scaling: A Continuous-Rate Alternative to Stepped Income Tax Brackets

detail.title: Logarithmic Tax Scaling: A Continuous-Rate Alternative to Stepped Income Tax Brackets
detail.abstract: The United States federal income tax imposes discrete marginal rate increases at legislatively defined income thresholds-a stepped bracket architecture that produces empirically documented behavioral distortions including income bunching, threshold avoidance, and compliance expenditure concentrated near bracket kink points. This paper introduces Logarithmic Tax Scaling (the "Ln-Scale") as a defined policy concept: a continuous-rate income tax architecture in which the marginal rate rises smoothly as a function of the natural logarithm of taxable income, eliminating bracket discontinuities by design. The proposed formula, T = k × ti × ln(1 + ti/c), produces a schedule that (1) imposes zero liability below a household income floor, (2) rises continuously to a statutory marginal cap, and (3) removes the rational behavioral incentive to manage income to thresholds. This paper reviews the theoretical foundation in Briskin (2013), the empirical literature on bunching behavior (Saez 2010; IZA 2018), specifies the formula and its parameters, and presents worked examples demonstrating revenue comparability with current law. The concept is introduced as a named term to facilitate entry into policy discourse.

title: Tailored Base-Surge Policies in Dual-Sourcing Inventory Systems with Demand Learning
affiliations: University of Illinois at Chicago - College of Business Administration and

detail.title: Tailored Base-Surge Policies in Dual-Sourcing Inventory Systems with Demand Learning
detail.abstract: We consider a periodic-review dual-sourcing inventory system, in which the expedited supplier is faster and more costly, while the regular supplier is slower and cheaper. Under full demand distributional information, it is well-known that the optimal policy is extremely complex but the celebrated Tailored Base-Surge (TBS) policy performs near optimally. Under such a policy, a constant order is placed at the regular source in each period, while the order placed at the expedited source follows a simple order-up-to rule. In this paper, we assume that the firm does not know the demand distribution a priori, and makes adaptive inventory ordering decisions in each period based only on the past sales (a.k.a. censored demand) data. The standard performance measure is regret, which is the cost difference between a feasible learning algorithm and the clairvoyant (full-information) benchmark. When the benchmark is chosen to be the (full-information) best Tailored Base-Surge policy, we develop the first nonparametric learning algorithm that admits a regret bound of O(√T(logT)3loglogT), which is provably tight up to a logarithmic factor. Leveraging the structure of this problem, our approach combines the power of bisection search and stochastic gradient descent and also involves a delicate high probability coupling argument between our and the clairvoyant optimal system dynamics.

title: THE SPACE™ DEFAULT VS MASTERY DOCTRINE™ Initiative Axis Determination of the Two Space™ States in Human Locomotor Dynamics™

detail.title: THE SPACE™ DEFAULT VS MASTERY DOCTRINE™ Initiative Axis Determination of the Two Space™ States in Human Locomotor Dynamics™
detail.abstract: This working paper presents the Space™ Default vs Mastery Doctrine™, a formally documented principle governing the two distinct states of the Space™ element within the UMAC™ taxonomy. Space™ appears at two opposite ends of the elemental development arc: as the default unconfirmed state every fighter occupies before the Herron Fold™ completes, and as the peak mastery state reached by the fighter who has inhabited, confirmed, and transcended all four elemental positions. The same initiative axis that governs the Water patience/predation bifurcation distinguishes these two Space™ states.

title: The Non-Wage Personal Income Ratio (NWPI Ratio): A Reproducible Metric for Tracking the Structural Composition of National Personal Income

detail.title: The Non-Wage Personal Income Ratio (NWPI Ratio): A Reproducible Metric for Tracking the Structural Composition of National Personal Income
detail.abstract: Standard economic indicators-median household income, GDP, unemployment-do not measure the structural composition of personal income: the proportion of total national personal income that flows from ownership rather than labor. This gap leaves policymakers without a standard metric to detect or monitor the gradual structural shift from a labor-income-dominant economy toward a capital-income-dominant one. This paper introduces the Non-Wage Personal Income Ratio (the NWPI Ratio) as a defined, reproducible metric derived directly from publicly available Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) National Income and Product Accounts (NIPA) data. The NWPI Ratio is defined as: (Personal Income-Compensation of Employees) ÷ Personal Income, using NIPA Table 2.1, Line 1 and Line 2. Calculated from BEA data, the broad NWPI Ratio rose from 30.2% in 1980 to 39.7% in 2024-a 9.5 percentage point structural shift over 44 years. A narrower ownership-income variant (isolating rental income, personal interest, and personal dividends) rose from approximately 17.9% to 21.0% over the same period. This paper defines the metric, specifies its data sources, presents the historical time series, addresses methodological limitations, and argues for its adoption as a standard indicator in economic opportunity analysis. The NWPI Ratio is introduced as a named term to facilitate entry into policy and academic discourse.

The Five Domain Framework™ provides secondary metabolic domain descriptors for each of the five UMAC™ elemental classes, grounding each element in its physical and metabolic expression. The Five Functions™-Apex™, Banshee™, Leviathan™, Valkyr™, and Onslaught™-are the asymptotic performance states of each elemental class: conceptually rigorous performance ceilings approached but never fully reached by fighters operating within their confirmed elemental class.

title: Explainable AI for Financial Risk Governance: A Systematic Literature Review

detail.title: Explainable AI for Financial Risk Governance: A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are being rapidly adopted across global financial institutions for credit risk assessment, fraud detection, anti-money laundering, and algorithmic trading. However, most high performing AI models are opaque “black-box” systems that make decisions without providing understandable reasons. This creates serious challenges for financial governance, regulatory compliance, and public trust. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a critical field that aims to make AI decisions transparent, interpretable, and auditable.

This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of research on XAI in financial risk governance. Following the PRISMA framework, we searched major academic databases including Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and SSRN, yielding 94 studies published between 2018 and 2026 for final analysis. We organize the findings into four major themes: (1) explainability techniques used in financial AI, (2) application domains in financial risk, (3) governance and regulatory challenges, and (4) enterprise-scale implementation barriers.

The review finds that SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) dominate the XAI literature in finance, yet significant gaps remain in their application at enterprise scale, in emerging market contexts, and within real time regulatory monitoring systems. Most reviewed studies focus on technical model performance and underemphasize governance structures, ethical accountability, and institutional deployment realities. This paper identifies six major research gaps and proposes a conceptual framework for enterprise grade explainable financial AI systems. The findings have direct implications for AI governance researchers, financial regulators, and technology strategists seeking to align AI systems with legal and ethical standards.

title: Optimal Dynamic Policies for the Multisecretary Problem with Many Candidates
affiliations: Northwestern University - Department of Operations and Northwestern University

detail.title: Optimal Dynamic Policies for the Multisecretary Problem with Many Candidates
detail.abstract: Many organizational decisions that involve sequential selection, such as hiring, venture funding, and grant allocation, are being reshaped by a widening mismatch between the size of the candidate pool and acceptance capacity. As participation frictions fall, this mismatch extends well beyond the environments in which fluid-regime calibrations were designed to operate, and the familiar rule of pinning selectivity to the ratio of remaining capacity to remaining candidates no longer provides the right guidance. We study this setting through the multisecretary problem in a large market regime with fixed capacity, in which the candidate pool grows while acceptance capacity remains fixed. Our main result is that the optimal dynamic policy is governed not by the physical number of remaining slots but by an effective capacity determined jointly by the physical capacity and the tail of the valuation distribution. This correction changes sign across tail classes. The optimal policy becomes more permissive in short-tailed environments, more selective in heavy-tailed environments, and coincides with the fluid-resolving heuristic in the light-tailed case. We characterize the optimal value and regret relative to the offline benchmark, and show why additive comparisons remain informative even when competitive ratios converge to one. We also fully characterize the static and dynamic certainty-equivalent policies and the optimal static policy, and establish that a simple tail-adjusted rule, obtained by replacing physical capacity with effective capacity in the dynamic threshold policy, is asymptotically optimal. Comparisons across policies show that the source of performance gains depends sharply on the shape of the distribution. In short-tailed environments and, more generally, under increasing hazard rates, most gains come from optimizing the static threshold, while the contributions of the effective-capacity correction and dynamic recalibration are smaller. In heavy-tailed environments and, more generally, under decreasing hazard rates, the main gains come from the effective-capacity correction together with dynamic recalibration.

title: AI Power at Tempo: Conversion, Harnesses, and Anticipatory Influence

detail.title: AI Power at Tempo: Conversion, Harnesses, and Anticipatory Influence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
This is the second in a series of issues papers developed in connection with AI: The New Face of Power, a book in progress under contract with Columbia University Press (2027). The series circulates selected ideas, cases, and frameworks as they are being developed and tested, and invites discussion. These papers are not excerpts from the book nor substitutes for its fuller argument and evidence.

As artificial intelligence moves from tool to infrastructure, the locus of organizational power shifts. Power no longer resides primarily in decisions made at the moment of choice. It resides as well in the systems that determine what is seen, what is prioritized, where work flows, and what happens by default before any formal decision is made.

This paper argues that AI constitutes a fourth face of power — pre-emptive power — exercised through anticipatory influence before any individual deliberates, alongside the three classical faces identified by Dahl, Bachrach and Baratz, and Lukes. Pre-emptive power operates through the harness: the socio-technical architecture surrounding and governing the conversion stack through which institutional purpose becomes machine-executable action. The paper identifies three interdependent harness domains: operational, institutional, and structural. Each is a site of managerial decision and potential failure, and introduces several new concepts to characterize their dynamics: replacement drift, building on Wu's mission drift; the AI cliff; encoded constraints; and constrained discretion. Together these give the framework analytical precision and practical application.

Harnesses are not passive architectures. Left ungoverned they default and degrade. A weak harness is one where constraints are underspecified, misaligned, or ungoverned. A strong harness is one where purpose is clearly encoded, authority clearly assigned, dependencies clearly understood, and learning loops active. Moore's strategic triangle, Christensen's value networks, Meadows' leverage points, Davenport's process transformation work, Simons's levers of control, and Mueller's ethics as architecture together give managers the frameworks to assess and strengthen harness readiness.

The framework is tested through eight cases spanning customer service, policing, social work, healthcare, transportation safety, software engineering, and geopolitical competition. The paper concludes with five managerial imperatives and a division of labor between leaders, who authorize and bound the system, and managers, who make it operate well.

title: A Dynamic Optimization Framework for Modular Mobile Automated Parcel Stations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Illinois at Chicago, Gustave Eiffel University and University of Illinois at Chicago

detail.title: A Dynamic Optimization Framework for Modular Mobile Automated Parcel Stations
detail.abstract: Urban e-commerce last-mile delivery increasingly relies on flexible, demand-responsive infrastructure to handle fluctuating pickup and delivery requests throughout the day. We propose Modular Mobile Automated Parcel Stations (MMAPS), a last-mile service in which autonomous locker pods (self-driving locker units) shuttle between terminal depots that act as supply hubs and customer-facing dwelling stations. Customers submit either a delivery request (parcel travels depot → customer) to receive an online order, or a pickup request (parcel travels customer → depot) to hand off an outbound parcel, and walk to a nearby dwelling station to complete the handoff. Pods can physically couple into platoons on shared road segments to reduce energy costs and decouple to serve different neighborhoods independently. We formulate a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) that jointly determines station activation, customer-to-station assignment within walking limits, pod routing with time windows and work-hour constraints, and platoon formation with size-dependent travelcost discounts. To handle same-day demand that arrives throughout the day, we introduce a rolling-horizon re optimization model that freezes executed actions and enforces a mid-point (MP) depot resupply for newly revealed deliveries served by en-route pods. Because the monolithic formulation is intractable for realistic instances, we develop a multi-stage solution workflow combining shareability-based customer clustering, relaxed MILP solves with warm starts, and cluster-based platoon refinement. Computational experiments on grid networks with up to 500 customers show that periodic re-planning reduces total cost by 13% on average relative to static planning, and that platooning provides an additional 2.2% saving on top of the dynamic re-planning gains.

title: Industrial Policy and Global Value Chains in India: Evaluating the Impact of PLI on Domestic Value Addition, Export Upgrading and Supplier Linkages

detail.title: Industrial Policy and Global Value Chains in India: Evaluating the Impact of PLI on Domestic Value Addition, Export Upgrading and Supplier Linkages

keywords: Industrial Policy; Global Value Chains; Production Linked Incentive; Domestic Value Addition; Export Upgrading; Supplier Linkages; Make in India; Electronics Manufacturing; India; PLI Scheme

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between India’s contemporary industrial policy and its integration into global value chains, with special reference to the Production Linked Incentive scheme. The study evaluates whether PLI-led manufacturing expansion is contributing to domestic value addition, export upgrading, and supplier-linkage development, or whether India’s GVC participation remains concentrated in assembly-oriented activities. Drawing on secondary data, official policy documents, and existing literature on GVC participation, domestic value-added trade, services, digitalisation, FDI, and electronics value chains, the paper argues that PLI has strengthened production and export performance in selected sectors, especially electronics and mobile phones. However, the deeper challenge remains the creation of domestic component ecosystems, technology transfer, MSME supplier participation, and higher domestic value capture. The paper concludes that India’s industrial policy must move beyond output incentives toward capability-building, supplier upgrading, services integration, and technology-focused GVC participation.

title: Trade Credit and Supply Chain Relationships
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - College of Business, Case Western Reserve University, Weatherhead School of Management, University of Texas at Austin - McCombs School of Business and University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign

detail.title: Trade Credit and Supply Chain Relationships
detail.abstract:
This paper examines how trade credit regulation influences supply chain relationships and network structure. Exploiting the implementation of France’s Loi de Modernisation de l’Economie (LME), which imposed strict limits on inter-firm payment durations, we employ a difference-in-differences design using granular global supply chain data. 

Contrary to the policy’s intended objective of stabilizing supply chains by alleviating supplier financial constraints, we find that mandated shorter payment terms significantly increase the likelihood of relationship termination, particularly for upstream links and low-margin suppliers. At the same time, the regulation stimulates the formation of new downstream relationships. These opposing forces lead to a structural reconfiguration of supply chains, resulting in shorter and flatter network structures. 

Our findings provide support for the incentive-provision view of trade credit, demonstrating that deferred payments function as a key relational governance mechanism rather than merely a source of short-term liquidity. When payment flexibility is constrained, firms strategically redesign their supply networks in response to weakened relational enforcement.

title: Public Support, Private Choices: The 2021 Child Tax Credit and Parental Spending Behavior

detail.title: Public Support, Private Choices: The 2021 Child Tax Credit and Parental Spending Behavior
detail.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms that link family income with child well-being is critical for designing effective child transfer policy. In this study, I examine household spending during the 2021 expanded Child Tax Credit (CTC) advance payment (AP) period to test theories of intrahousehold allocation decision-making. I argue that examining parents' spending on vice goods-goods they value, but which may harm children-can provide a unique window into parental motivations. I analyze data from the NielsenIQ Consumer Panel (NCP) using a matched two-way fixed effects design to estimate the causal effect of CTC advance payments on consumption of vice goods. My results suggest that parents' vice consumption did not increase in response to advance payment of the expanded CTC. This paper provides insight into how parents balance self-interest and altruism when making spending decisions. These insights can inform the design of child-focused transfer policies by suggesting whether unrestricted cash transfers are an effective means of improving children's well-being.

detail.abstract:
Many people know Colin Rule as a pioneer of online dispute resolution.  Fewer people probably appreciate the full breadth of his contributions over the last three decades. This article reviews Rule’s work as a builder of dispute resolution systems, writer, educator, entrepreneur, and institutional leader.  It highlights recurring themes in his career and scholarship, including trust, fairness, usability, access to justice, and the need to keep human judgment at the center of technological innovation.

Drawing on Real Practice Systems Theory, the article also examines how Rule developed his distinctive practice system grounded in values, experimentation, practical usefulness, and sustained commitment.   His career helps illuminate the history of ODR as well as future opportunities and risks facing dispute resolution in the age of artificial intelligence.

title: When Do Forecasts Create More Value? A Bayesian Newsvendor Perspective
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics

detail.title: When Do Forecasts Create More Value? A Bayesian Newsvendor Perspective

publicationDetails.detailsText: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper No. 2026/006
publicationDetails.journalName: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Problem definition: We study how forecast information creates economic value in Bayesian newsvendor decisions. We focus on the information structure induced by the forecast signal rather than treating it only as a point prediction. Academic/practical relevance: In practice, forecasts can induce a wide variety of information structures. Yet, studies that link these structures to inventory decisions have focused on a limited set of benchmark structures, thereby limiting firms' capacity to evaluate and select forecast information effectively. Methodology: We develop a Bayesian framework that models the full information structure induced by a forecast signal and estimates the resulting economic value. The framework allows for structures with non-zero conditional mean errors, heavy-tailed noise, heteroscedasticity, and standard benchmarks. Results: The value of forecast information depends jointly on forecast responsiveness and noise dispersion, not on noise dispersion alone. Consequently, a forecast with larger raw errors can be more valuable if it is more responsive to demand. Within homoscedastic noise families (Normal and Laplace), the ratio of noise dispersion to forecast responsiveness is sufficient to compare forecast models by economic value, whereas standard accuracy measures can misrank them. Across noise families, this ratio alone is no longer sufficient, but when combined with the critical fractile, it can identify which model yields greater value. Managerial implications: Rather than relying solely on accuracy, managers should evaluate forecast models as information structures. This requires measuring forecast responsiveness, not just noise dispersion, and avoiding homoscedastic Normal noise assumptions without validation. Failure to do so can lead managers to select lower-value forecasts, overestimate the value of forecast adoption, and forfeit attainable forecast value.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the Universal Metabolic Attrition Complex (UMAC), a constraint-satisfaction framework for classifying competitive martial identity. The central claim is structural: determining a fighter’s stable behavioral configuration under sustained competitive constraint is formally isomorphic to the protein folding problem as articulated by Anfinsen’s Dogma (1972) and operationalized at scale by AlphaFold (2024). In both domains, an identity-encoding sequence — amino acids in proteins, an “attrition archetype” in fighters — yields, under defined environmental constraints, a stable configuration via free-energy minimization.
From this isomorphism the paper develops the Herron Identity Convergence Principle: the attrition archetype contains all information required to determine confirmed elemental rank. The five-element partition is derived from the Platonic-solid completeness proof — exactly five regular convex polyhedra exist in three-dimensional Euclidean space — so elemental completeness is structurally necessary rather than stylistically chosen. The framework specifies twelve attrition archetypes mapped to four elemental positions plus a meta-position, five metabolic energy systems governed by an adaptive meta-allocator, four principles of territorial intelligence, six formally named paradoxes, and twelve counter-action architectures presented as a complete basis set.
Cross-system convergence analysis across twelve independent classification traditions (Western and Vedic zodiacs, Xing Yi Quan’s twelve animals, the Enneagram, MBTI, and others dating from c.1500 BCE) provides observational support for the four-by-three substructure, consistent with the four-cluster personality typology reported by Gerlach et al. (2018, n≈1.5M). The paper distinguishes empirically confirmed claims, strongly inferred claims, and theoretical extrapolations.

This study provides a critical lens for understanding and optimizing administrative efficacy in faith-based organizations.

title:
Constitutionalism Versus Traditional Authority: The Role of the Constitution in the Institutionalisation of Authority in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq 
A Critical and Analytical Study

detail.title:
Constitutionalism Versus Traditional Authority: The Role of the Constitution in the Institutionalisation of Authority in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq 
A Critical and Analytical Study
detail.abstract:
One of the fundamental questions in the political philosophy of the constitution is why states require a written constitution or legal-rational authority. A common answer is that a written constitution serves to restrain the emergence of a Leviathan, to establish rational and institutional authority, and to safeguard fundamental rights and freedoms. From this perspective, Constitutionalism is conceived as a framework for limiting political power and institutionalizing Authority, rather than allowing the persistence of traditional or despotic forms of rule. One of the primary mechanisms for achieving the institutionalization of authority is the existence of a modern constitution, functioning as the highest and most legitimate source of legal and political order.

However, the Kurdistan Region of Iraq has failed to develop such a model of rational constitutional governance over the past three decades. Despite the provisions of the 2005 Iraqi Constitution, which granted the Region the right to adopt its own constitution, political authority in the Region has remained dominated by traditional structures and Partocratic rule. This failure to institutionalize authority has contributed to the erosion of democratic practices, human rights, and the rule of law in the Region.

This study adopts a critical and analytical approach to examine the nature of authority in the Kurdistan Region. It assumes that the adoption of a written constitution is essential for the institutionalization of constitutional authority, shaping the functioning of the legislative, executive, and judicial branches.

title: ESGWave: Sustainability, Finance and the Future of Business

detail.title: ESGWave: Sustainability, Finance and the Future of Business
detail.abstract:
This article examines the growing impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles on business operations and performance, positioning sustainability as a critical determinant of corporate success in the global economy today. It explores how the global shift toward sustainable finance driven by financial institutions, regulatory frameworks, and international commitments has redefined access to capital, making ESG compliance an essential criterion for businesses seeking funding through loans, private equity, and capital markets.

In addition, the article evaluates the relationship between sustainability and profitability, emphasizing how evolving consumer preferences, investor expectations, and workforce dynamics are influencing business outcomes. The article concludes that the ESG wave is not merely a trend but a structural shift, compelling businesses to integrate sustainability into their core strategies to ensure resilience, competitiveness, and sustainable growth.

title: When the Agent Can Die: Contract Theory with Absorbing Exit
affiliations: Southern Illinois University - Department of Economics

detail.title: When the Agent Can Die: Contract Theory with Absorbing Exit
detail.abstract: Every canonical principal-agent model assumes the agent persists at the boundary. This paper replaces the reflecting boundary with an absorbing one, where the agent who crosses is gone permanently. A survival wedge emerges: a region of the state space where the agent is alive but every deterrent punishment is also lethal, so no mechanism can operate. Optimal mechanisms front-load discipline, and the value function carries a survival premium near the boundary, the shadow price on the constraint that enforceable actions must be survivable. Golden parachutes emerge as the residual of front-loaded enforcement insurance, not as managerial rent extraction. The welfare cost of absorbing exit equals the integrated survival premium. The same object underlies endogenous risk premia near intermediary equity constraints in the macro-finance literature. The general result requires three assumptions and one intermediate-value argument. Four canonical setups verify it: static moral hazard (Holmström 1979; Innes 1990), dynamic moral hazard (DeMarzo and Sannikov 2006), relational contracting (Levin 2003), and optimal delegation (Holmström 1984).

title: 60 Hours Belonging to No One

detail.title: 60 Hours Belonging to No One
detail.abstract: The Invisible Problem Imagine this situation: a member of your team receives a task. The agreed estimate is 40 horas. Weeks later, when the task is complete, the actual time invested has been 200 horas. The difference, 160 horas, does not disappear. And nobody quite knows what to do with it. This uncertainty is the origin of a chain of injustices that, in many teams, repeats itself silently and systematically. Not out of anyone's ill will, but because the rules used to manage work are not designed to handle that complexity. This article analyses that problem, formulates it precisely and proposes a compensation system that aligns team incentives in a fair and sustainable way. It also addresses the human cost of leaving it unresolved, and why that cost is greater today than ever before.

detail.abstract: This article examines the form of the political standard of the third millennium as a derivative of the laws of nature and the cosmic model, in which the evolution of civilisation is determined not by political agreements but by the natural mechanism of the mutation of the genetics of the masses, the succession of leaders and reformers, and the readiness of the state to fulfil its obligations toward the human being, the family, and the living environment. On the basis of this model, a list of the obligations of the state of the third millennium is formedfrom the digital judicial process and pre-trial investigation to the personalised security channel for every citizen, the free network resource, and a new economic regulator through digital governmentand a digital architecture for their fulfilment is proposed, comprising machine-readable laws of nature (NLCL), the planetary e-Discovery ecosystem, neurosymbolic pipelines, and the Digital Warrant mechanism. The model of the ecology of life is disclosed as a complex of the natural guarantees of civilisation: unified statehood, a resource of regeneration, an institute of open convergent knowledge, genetic security, longevity, and climatically protected territories governed by the Scientific Council of the Planet through the Centralised Analytical Centre (CAC). The operational platform of this model is the integration of CAC, the personalised working desk of the human being, the genetic passport with three-layer protection, and a system of regeneration that together eliminate the causes of the premature wear of the human being and translate longevity from a medical task into a production cycle of a healthy civilisation. It is demonstrated that the transmission of accumulated historical layers of conflicts and injustices to the Scientific Council of the Planet through CAC ensures the reading of truth on the basis of the laws of nature and creates an architecture of restorative justicefor families, peoples, and states.
